plan.summary: Most listings are basically right: pins sit a median 56 m from the shop's own address, 99.6% of time zones are correct, 221 of 222 chain hours match the chains' own feeds, and about 95% of the 4,008 cigar-named public listings are real cigar shops or lounges. The biggest risks are not in the core data. They are in the plumbing and the edges: the importer and the storefront sweep undo fixes (4 website closures, Redland confirmed closed, will come back at the next import). 234 map-only hours are wrong for about half the listings that show them. Shops that moved are still listed at the old address (a combined pool of 92 phone-and-name pairs, 173 listings, about 18 confirmed stale). About 150-250 public listings are not shops at all. Taken-over domains put gambling links and pictures on real shops' cards. Dense metros also have a silent 300-row cap that drops nearby shops (131 listings can't be found from their own door). Closure detection is the weakest area: a dead website is not evidence (11 of 11 sampled were open), and state licence registries, free for 38% of listings, are the only free signal that caught a closure the other checks missed.

sweeps.name: Make fixes stick: one field-ownership model in the importer, plus a re-import test
sweeps.area: cross-area (closures, location, names, contact, amenities, chains, licences)
sweeps.problem: Jobs undo each other's work. storefrontCheck reset Redland Cigar Co (#2585, closed per its own site) from 'closed' back to 'yes' 6 minutes after closureCheck closed it. At the next import, visible = 1 and operating_status = 'open', so the shop returns to the map as open. The same applies to #11014, #8767 and #18397. chainCheck writes the non-standard operating_status 'closed', so its 7 closures never appear in the staff Closures queue. The importer also overwrites name, address, phone and lat/lng on every unclaimed row, even staff_edited ones. has_lounge can only go up (GREATEST), and tags are written only on insert. Any rename, move, pin, phone or badge fix is therefore undone at the next deploy.
sweeps.scale: Measured: 4 website closures and 7 chain closures at risk today, and all 7,431 public rows exposed to future reverts. Six auditors each proposed their own source column for the same UPDATE statement. The critic confirmed the Redland timestamps.
sweeps.method:
Ship in two steps.

Step A, in 2-3 hours:
- storefrontCheck skips any row whose storefront is 'closed' or 'duplicate', or whose operating_status is 'permanently_closed' or 'likely_closed'.
- The importer treats our own permanently_closed as binding, and stops writing the source's 'open' over a closure we set.
- chainCheck writes 'permanently_closed' instead of 'closed'.
- From a reviewed file, set #2585 and #11014 closed again. Send #8767 Boatyard (probably open; see rank 7) and #18397 to a person.

Step B:
- Add one per-field provenance map to stores, covering name, address block, lat/lng, phone, website, hours, amenities and tags. Values: directory, rule, website, chain, registry, geocode, staff, owner.
- Add a store_edits log that records field, before, after, job, and time.
- The importer writes a field only when its source is 'directory'. It recomputes the timezone whenever the state or pin changes, and recomputes tags and badges only for directory-owned rows.
- Extend scratchpad test_reimport.js: seed a website closure, a chain closure, a report closure, a renamed row, a moved pin, a staff phone and a removed lounge badge. Run storefrontCheck and a forced import, and assert that every one survives.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: A wrong closure also becomes sticky, so #8767 and #18397 go to a person first. Backfill every existing row as 'directory' so nothing changes until a sweep writes. The re-import test must pass before any other sweep in this plan is applied.
sweeps.effort: Step A 2-3 h. Step B about 1.5 days, including the log and the test.

sweeps.name: Time zones from county lines, not longitude rules
sweeps.problem: The longitude rules in storeHours.splitState (lines 39-47) put split-state towns on the wrong clock. The Open/Closed badge is then an hour off at both ends of the day. Examples: Burns Tobacconist in Chattanooga shows 'Open until 7pm' from 7 to 8pm Eastern while its door is locked; Mandan ND is on Mountain time; Houghton and Negaunee MI are on Central; Michigan City IN and Glasgow KY are on Eastern.
sweeps.scale: Measured: 26 (hours auditor) to 31 (location auditor) public listings. These are the same rows found two ways: Chattanooga/East Ridge/Lakesite 10-12, MI Upper Peninsula 5, south-central KY 4-5, La Porte County 2, Mandan, Crossville and Phenix City 1 each, and 2-5 wrong-state records. 10-11 of them have hours today. fillTimezones only fills NULLs, so fixing the code alone would not correct them.
sweeps.method: Replace splitState with a county lookup: Census county polygons plus the 49 CFR 71 split-county list, or a vendored tz-lookup restricted to US zones. Fall back to the state rule when the lookup returns a non-US zone (Houlton ME, Calais ME and Sault Ste. Marie come back as Canadian). Add a manual Eastern override for Phenix City and Russell County AL: legally Central, but it keeps Columbus GA time. Run a one-off recompute of every row, not just NULLs, and change only rows whose UTC offset actually differs. Log old and new values. Add self-tests for every town named above. Leave the 3 rows whose pin and state disagree for rank 9.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: A wrong zone shifts a whole town by an hour. Review the full diff (about 30 rows) before applying. Watford City ND stays Central unless checked.
sweeps.effort: 3-4 h build, 30 min review

sweeps.name: Map-only hours: stop asserting Open/Closed, re-read the shops that publish hours, and stop inventing Closed days
sweeps.problem: Hours that come only from OpenStreetMap look exactly as authoritative as hours read from the shop's own site, yet about half are wrong. Examples: Rich's Cigar Store Pearl (#10091) shows Mon-Sat 10-6 while the shop opens only Mon/Wed/Fri 1:30-4. Charles P Stanley shows Sat 1pm-1:30am. Mike's Cigars shows its customer-service line. A Closed day is also inferred whenever the mapper left the day out (Merced shows Sun Closed; aggregators say it opens 9-7). El Septimo Hollywood (#4061) shows hours but is marked CLOSED on Yelp.
sweeps.scale: 234 public listings carry map hours. Measured: 5 of 11 in a random draw were wrong and 1 looked closed. 33 of 71 overlap cases differed from the shop's site, 14 of 71 badly. Estimate: about 105-130 wrong on some day. 41 have an inferred Closed day. 45 have a dead website. 32 have a readable hours block on their own site already on disk.
sweeps.method:
(a) Product change: for rows where hours_source is null, show the hours as 'from OpenStreetMap, not confirmed', with no green or grey badge. Keep these rows out of 'Open now', or give them a 'probably open' label.
(b) Stop writing Closed for days the OSM tag omits; show them as unknown.
(c) Re-run decide on the 32 with new rules: 'Store' lines outrank Phone, Customer service and Office lines; read '&'/comma day lists and 'Closed all other days'; accept address-tied blocks. Review, then apply with hours_source='website'.
(d) Send map-hours rows with a dead site and an OSM edit older than 2 years to the closure queue as review items, never hidden automatically.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: One decision: drop the badge for unverified map hours, or keep it with a qualifier. Recommended: drop it.
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: Parts (a), (b) and (d) only remove a claim, never add one. Part (c) could pick up a sister branch's block, so it uses the review-file flow and the sibling-town guard from rank 6.
sweeps.effort: 1 day, plus 1-2 h review

sweeps.name: Moved shops and closed branches (one sweep owns the whole pool)
sweeps.problem: When a shop moves or shuts one branch, the old address often stays public next to the new one, or instead of it. Customers drive to an empty storefront. The closures, duplicates, location and chains auditors each proposed a sweep over what is largely the same pool.
sweeps.method:
Build candidates from all five pools, deduplicated by listing id. For each group, reuse the hours sweep's collect step (homepage plus up to 3 contact or locations pages, rendered for JS sites), JSON-LD PostalAddress, WPSL and chain feeds, and the licence holder's current address once rank 11 exists.

Match house number first. Then compare the street name after dedupeListings.normalizeAddress, allowing an edit distance of 1 so 'Green' matches 'Greene'.

Verdicts:
- The site says moved or new location and names one street: hide the other listing with storefront='moved' and a pointer.
- The site works, names the business, publishes full addresses, at least as many as the listings we keep, and never mentions B's house number: hide B.
- The site names a new street in B's town that no listing has: propose an address change, geocoded (Census or Nominatim, rank 9 rules).
- Both addresses named: keep both.
- No readable site: no action.

Write a decisions file. Apply with --from reviewed --confirm.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: One decision: when the new address is not listed yet (Churchill's Glendale), edit the old row in place or create a new row and hide the old one.
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: The risk is hiding a real second branch. Point Break Cigars has 5 Key West stores on one phone, and its site spells '403 Green St'. Guardrails: house-number matching, the address-coverage rule, and a phone match or explicit moved wording. Chains with more than 10 locations need their locator feed. Every decision is reviewed, and every hide is reversible, with a pointer. Depends on rank 1, so that address edits survive re-import.
sweeps.effort: 1.5 days build, about 1 h crawl, 2-3 h review

sweeps.name: Cigar search counts only visible stores, and never shows $0.00
sweeps.problem: The cigar list, city/state, price and in-stock filters join inventory without checking stores.visible. Stock at closed, duplicate and not-retail listings therefore counts. Example: Kristoff Sumatra (cigar 176) shows '1 store, from $200', yet its 'Where to find it' list is empty; the stock belongs to #1056, hidden as not_retail. Hoyo Excalibur counts closed #2013 Anthony's. /availability also treats a $0 price as a real price, so the cigar page prints '$0.00' for shops that publish no price.
sweeps.scale: Measured: 4 hidden listings hold 2,790 in-stock rows across 741 cigar lines. For 238 of those lines, every stocked store is hidden. 254 fully unpriced lines sit on 11 public listings (Cypress Cigars alone has 148).
sweeps.method: In cigars.js (list, /followed, city/state, min/max price, in_stock_only, price-comparison), smoke-list.js and users.js, join stores with s.visible = 1. Use MIN(NULLIF(price,0)). In /availability, count only prices above 0 and otherwise show 'price not listed'. When any job or staff action hides a listing, set its source='web' rows to in_stock=0, without deleting them. One-off for the 4 hidden listings. Test: for every one of the 741 lines, store_count equals the length of /availability.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: Very low. Hidden stores are already excluded from store lists and from 'Where to find it'. Unhiding a listing plus the next menu read restores its rows.
sweeps.effort: 2-3 h including tests

sweeps.name: Re-audit the 1,077 website-sourced hours: wrong site, sister branch, host venue, office line, expired season, typos
sweeps.needs_from_mason: One decision: when a seasonal window lapses with no new season posted, show the last schedule with a warning or clear it.
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: The risk is clearing hours that are right: House of Cigar and Anthony's name sibling towns but are correct. Guardrails: review only, never clear automatically. A cleared listing shows 'Hours not listed', which is never a wrong Closed. Extend the parser self-tests with every example above.
sweeps.effort: 1.5-2 days build, 2-3 h review

sweeps.name: Taken-over, parked and redirected links; closure reader trusts only the shop's own page
sweeps.problem:
Lapsed shop domains now serve gambling, spam or for-sale pages. linkCheck rates them 'ok', and the page links and labels the destination.
- Gambling: puffnstuffcigars.com goes to gamebaidoithuong.property; havanaonhudson.com goes to a betting site.
- The same takeovers supply thumbnails: Mike's Cigar Room shows an Indonesian gambling banner and 82nd Ave Tobacco a bikini slot-machine image.
- Parked: GoDaddy /lander pages (Paradise Cigars, Screaming Eagle) pass as working.
- The closure reader followed a redirect to a political blog and hid a trading shop, #8767 Boatyard Tobacco.
- Shopify 402 'store unavailable' pages are rated 'blocked', which counts as working.
sweeps.method:
Extend linkCheck, forcing a recheck of every public website. New verdicts:
- 'elsewhere': the final registrable domain differs and the destination does not name the shop (distinctive name token in title, og:site_name or JSON-LD, or our phone, or our street number).
- 'hijacked': 2 or more gambling terms in the title or first 64 KB, and no cigar or tobacco word.
- 'parked': a /lander stub, a for-sale host, or a 'Resources and Information' template.
- 'store_unavailable': HTTP 402.
All four count as dead.

Consumers:
- websiteInfo follows website_final_url only on a same-business verdict.
- closureCheck returns no opinion when the final domain differs, unless the page names the shop.
- Add maps.apple.com, g.co, maps.app.goo.gl, share.google, tinyurl, bit.ly and parking hosts to NOT_THE_SHOPS_SITE.
- Hijacked or parked domains lose their thumbnail and any website hours.
- A parked or hijacked own-domain link is a weak likely_closed signal, queued for staff and never auto-hidden.
- Re-run the 4 existing website closures (Boatyard is probably a reopen).

Deep links: when a path returns 404 but the root works and names a single-location shop, store the root. Chain branch pages instead go to chainCheck as closed-branch leads.

Optional: run RDAP on dead roots, which feeds rank 13.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: One decision: should a parked or hijacked own-domain count as a weak closure signal (about 90 listings would enter the queue)?
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: The risk is a real rebrand redirect losing its link (stogiepairing.com to stogiesftmyers.com). Guardrails: a phone or address match on the destination passes; an allow-list covers proven parent redirects (tobaccoconnection.net to jacksonbevco.com, cheaptobaccousa.com to wildbillstobacco.com); casino-resort lounges need the gambling words in the title and the shop's name absent from it. Every 'elsewhere' verdict is reviewed. A false positive hides only a link, never a shop.
sweeps.effort: 1-1.5 days build, 30 min run, about 2 h review

sweeps.name: Non-shop purge, plus the classifier and storefront rule fixes that let them through
sweeps.area: relevance / names / amenities / images / contact / duplicates
sweeps.problem:
Some public 'shops' are places a customer can't buy cigars:
- Makers, head offices and landmarks: R.J. Reynolds x5, Lorillard, Liggett and Myers, Universal Leaf.
- Places that aren't shops: a trail parking lot, an RV lot, a marina, a union hall, a state office, an ATF office.
- Anti-smoking campaigns: Tobacco Free Sarpy, 'Tobacco 21'.
- Online-only sellers tagged 'Walk-in Humidor': Humidors Direct, Luxury Cigar Humidors, Grand Humidors.
- Mobile or event lounges with a pin: 17 by name.
- Private homes and joke check-ins: 'Monica Lewinsky Cigar Lounge', backyard 'lounges'.
- Head shops and a plumber, public because 'pipe' scores as tobacco: Pipe Dreams Sanford, pipedreamsplumb.com.
- Vape and kava lounges, and a vape review site, public through the 'cigarette' or 'lounge' domain bonus.
- Hookah restaurants and corner smoke shops typed cigar_lounge with a Lounge badge: Lava Hookah.
- Online warehouses sharing a door: Thompson/CI, Cigars Direct.
In the other direction, storefrontCheck lets 'Co', 'Company' or 'House' count as a premises word by itself.
sweeps.method:
1) Name and category pass. Mark storefront not_retail or online_only, with a reason, when a known maker or HQ, union, association, government, trail, RV, marina, landmark, 'No Public Sales' or event/mobile name coincides with an Overture category such as corporate_office, tobacco_company, landmark, coworking, hiking_trail, central_government_office, party_and_event_planning or wholesaler. Also cover humidor web catalogues, toll-free rows whose site is a brand, and Meta rows with no phone, no site and a residential or missing street plus a possessive first name or 'backyard'/'porch'.
2) Classifier (osm.classify, buildDirectory):
- the domain bonus uses cigar(?!et) and counts 'lounge' only with a cigar word;
- add vapes, kava, 710, dab, bong, hydro, headshop, 'peace pipe' and 'pipe dreams' to the strong negatives;
- type cigar_lounge (and the Lounge tag) only with cigar vocabulary, never from the cigar_bar category when the name says smoke, vape, mart or deli.
3) storefrontCheck: co/company/house alone is no longer enough off the retail allow-list.
Run a dry-run diff of public-to-hidden flips with the triggering rule, and review it. Flips toward public go to rank 25, not live.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Two decisions: are members-only lounges badged or hidden (badge recommended), and are head shops, pipe-and-vape shops and hookah lounges in scope?
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: The risk is hiding a factory that sells retail (J.C. Newman, Corona Cigar Co, Tampa factories) or a real tobacconist named 'Pipe'. Guardrails: never auto-hide a row whose name has a cigar or brand word and a retail category; claimed and staff_edited rows are untouched; staff review every row; every hide is written as a storefront reason so the importer honours it. Self-tests: #5413, #22109 and #12898 must stay; #4581, #6466 and #10186 must go. Run this before rank 12, because a complete distance-first list surfaces these rows in dense metros. Include #41488 Nat Sherman Townhouse (closed 2020) and #37650 Cigars & Roses in the queue.
sweeps.effort: 1-1.5 days build, 2-3 h review

sweeps.name: Pins, states and foreign records
sweeps.problem: Some pins sit far from the shop's own address: Tobacco Junction of Marshall is 404 km off; Amsterdam Tobacco House (Upper West Side) is pinned on Long Island; Greystone Cigars is 40 km off. Some listings are filed under the wrong state: Black Jack's Cigar Lounge in El Paso's Hotel Paso del Norte is listed and pinned in New London CT; Sam Hill's (Prescott AZ) is listed in Gallup NM; Tobacco Country (Greenwood LA) is listed as TX. Some are foreign: La Casa del Habano in Windsor, Ontario, and a Lebanese 'Tobacco Bar'. In 35 same-address twin pairs the pins are more than 300 m apart, so a merge must pick the right pin.
sweeps.scale: Measured: 153 public pins more than 1 km from the Census geocode of their own address (47 more than 5 km, 4 more than 50 km). On ordinary street addresses, 11 of 11 sampled disagreements had the pin wrong. On highway-style addresses the geocoder itself is wrong about 40% of the time. Estimate: 100-130 real pin errors. Also 17 wrong-state or foreign rows (4 confirmed), 13 ZIP/state contradictions and 9 area-code conflicts (the same rows, detected by phone).
sweeps.method:
1) Run the Census batch geocoder (free, 10k rows per request) over every public address. Take a second opinion from Nominatim for disagreements over 1 km. Use chain-feed coordinates only when the feed's address equals ours.
2) Move a pin automatically only when all of these hold: an ordinary street (not US-/SR-/FM/Hwy/Route); a Census exact match plus a Nominatim house-level match within 250 m of each other; both more than 1 km from the pin; a move of at most 50 km; and the address backed by the shop's site, a chain feed or the geocoder's ZIP. Everything else goes to review.
3) State: change it only when the ZIP prefix and one more signal (a detailed Census boundary, the area code, or GeoNames city-in-state) agree on the same other state. Then re-geocode the row and recompute its timezone.
4) Foreign records (+961, Canadian postcode or area code) and records with three or more contradictions (Cigar Crafted, Cigar Vibes, Mort's, Vip smoke) become hidden after review.
5) Build-time guards: buildDirectory checks Overture's region against the ZIP and the pin; fetchOsmStores keeps addr:state and addr:postcode.
Write location_source='geocode' and keep the previous coordinates.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Decide whether foreign and self-contradicting records are hidden or repaired.
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: The risk is moving a pin to an old address the shop has left. Run rank 4 first, and send addresses the site disputes to review. Guardrails: highway exclusion; two geocoders must agree; never act on a foreign phone alone (Puro Estilo is a real Bethlehem PA seller); hand-review 30 decisions before applying; claimed and owner rows are untouched. Needs rank 1.
sweeps.effort: 1.5 days build, 1 h run, 2-3 h review

sweeps.name: Likely-closed flag: clean its inputs, extend it to stale OSM pins, and warn shoppers
sweeps.problem: The likely-closed flag rests on weak links, and shoppers never see it. 12 of the 45 flagged listings rest only on a dead platform or directory link (business.site, cigarplaces.com), and two rows are one shop (Tin Can #29843/#29844). Torch Cigar Lounge was flagged but is open. Holy Smokes (#27021) is truly closed, yet its card looks normal. Meanwhile, OSM-only pins with no phone, no website and often no street are never checked at all: Edward's Pipe & Tobacco in Los Altos, closed since 2025, is still public.
sweeps.scale: Measured: 45 public listings flagged likely_closed (1 of 3 sampled was closed). 651 public listings have no website and no phone. The strongest subset is 46: OSM-only, last edited before 2020, with no Overture record within 150 m (1 of 2 checked was closed). 268 more public listings have no address, no phone and no website (location auditor; these overlap).
sweeps.method:
1) Treat dead links on platform or directory hosts as 'no website'.
2) Merge duplicates before flagging.
3) New rule: flag likely_closed when a listing is OSM-only, with no phone, website or hours, last edited on OSM before 2020 (Overpass out meta; change the fetch to 'out center meta'), and no Overture cigar or tobacco record within 150 m.
4) On a likely_closed card, drop the 'Open now' badge and show 'We couldn't confirm this shop is still open. Call or check before you go.'
5) Clear the flag automatically when the listing gains a phone, a working site or hours.
6) Sort the staff queue by strength of evidence.
Never auto-hide from this signal.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: One decision: may a public caveat appear on likely-closed listings? Recommended yes.
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: A neutral caveat on a live shop (Torch, Tin Can) could cost it a visit. Guardrails: neutral wording, never hide, and clear the flag automatically on new contact data.
sweeps.effort: Half a day

sweeps.name: State licence registries: join, verify, and queue closures, renames and moves
sweeps.problem:
No job uses the free tobacco-retailer licence registries, yet they caught what Overture, the website check and the contact check missed.
- Winston's Cigar Lounge in Houston (#5465) closed on 12 January after 63 years. Its TX permit ended that day, and the listing is public and marked open.
- The Smoking Lamp in Allen TX (#7233) now trades as Allen Cigar Lounge, at the same suite with the same phone.
- Churchill Cigar Lounge in San Diego (#2377) is now Royal Cigar Lounge.
- Creekside (#2993) and Carlos Cabeza (#26226) moved, and the registries give the new addresses.
sweeps.method:
1) licenceSync job: load the 9 free sources (NYC DCWP, NYS Tax and DOH, TX Comptroller, FL DBPR, CA CDTFA, PA DOR, Chicago BACP, WA LCB) into server/data/licences.json.gz, refreshed monthly.
2) Join on phone; or ZIP/town plus house number plus a shared street word; or matching suites; or within 60 m with the names agreeing. Compare names on distinctive words only, without the town word.
3) Stamp last_verified_at wherever an active licence matches both address and name.
4) Queues, which never write visibility:
- (a) Replaced: another business's active licence at our suite or phone, with name similarity below 0.8. Propose that business's trading name.
- (b) Moved: the same holder is now active elsewhere in town, and the old licence ended within 60 days of the new one starting. Feed this to rank 4.
- (c) Closed: the licence ended at least 60 days ago with a real end date, plus one independent signal. Write likely_closed with the reason.
Skip TX INACTIVE permits with no end date, listings whose own site gave hours in the last 30 days, and claimed or staff rows.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Confirm that registry evidence only flags and never hides. Name and address changes need rank 1. Decide whether NYC smoke shops are exempt from lapse flags (many trade without a licence).
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: The risk is renaming or closing an open shop: 3 of 12 lapses were open (Stogies, BlackHouse, Manhattan Tobacco). Guardrails: flag only; a 60-day lag allowance; 'no website' does not count as a second signal; ignore the stale NY DOH (January) and WA (February) lists for closures; staff check the shop's site or Yelp before approving; keep the old name as a search alias.
sweeps.effort: 1.5-2 days for the sync, 1 day for the queues, 2-3 h review

sweeps.name: Complete search results: distance first, a hard radius, exact counts, Open now on the full set
sweeps.problem: GET /stores sorts by a feed-size and confidence key, applies LIMIT 300, and only then cuts to the radius, sorts by distance and filters Open now. In dense metros the list drops shops a few blocks away while showing shops 49 miles out, and the page counts only what it kept, so nothing says the list is incomplete. Missing in live API responses: Manhattan Tobacco at 0.9 mi from Midtown, Tap That Ash in Wilton Manors, and at 100 mi Davidoff Madison Ave and Jhaveri Cigar Stand.
sweeps.scale:
Measured by replay, which matched the live API id for id:
- 131 public listings can't be found from their own door at 50 mi (1,032 at 100 mi).
- In 949 of 7,431 locations the 50-mi search overflows the cap.
- Recall is 93.5% at 50 mi and 73.1% at 100 mi.
- Midtown returns 272 of 364 within 50 mi.
- Open now loses 41 of 983 open shops at 50 mi and 397 of 1,831 at 100 mi.
- 82% of listings have no hours and silently never appear under Open now.
sweeps.method:
When lat/lng are given:
- Select light columns inside the bbox prefilter with every SQL filter applied, and keep rows whose haversine distance (computed in SQL) is within the radius. Apply no LIMIT to this candidate set; the worst case today is 743 rows.
- Run openStatus over the full set.
- Sort by distance, then id.
- Return total plus one page of about 60 with 'Show more', hydrating ratings and inventory only for that page.
- Cap the radius at 100 mi, and set a ceiling (e.g. 5,000) that answers 'narrow your search' instead of truncating silently.
- The page shows '364 shops within 50 mi' and, under Open now, 'N more nearby have no hours on file'.
- Add a recall monitor to CI or run it nightly: 62 metros x 4 radii x filters, requiring 100% recall (work/ranking m1-m3.js already do this).
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Two decisions: keep the 100-mi option, and how Featured/Partner placement appears inside a radius (the plans promise top placement).
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: The list now also surfaces low-confidence rows the cap used to hide (131 at 50 mi, mostly 0.55 tobacco_shop, including non-shops). Run rank 8 on the 8 affected metros first. Diff the first 30 cards before and after for Midtown, Brooklyn, Newark, Long Island, DC, Baltimore, Fort Lauderdale and LA.
sweeps.effort: 1.5 days, plus 1 h before/after review

sweeps.name: Claim safety gate (must ship before SMTP is switched on)
sweeps.problem:
Instant claim trusts the domain of the stored website and nothing else.
- It never checks website status, where the site redirects, or when the domain was registered.
- rootDomain keeps only two labels, so any .com.au, .co.uk, *.wi.us or @yahoo.com mailbox 'owns' a listing.
- One chain or directory mailbox can claim every listing that shares its domain, because contact_email comes from the request and account emails are never checked.
- Staff approval re-publishes hidden closed or duplicate rows with a verified badge (#10022 Broadway Cigar is confirmed closed).
- A claim can't be revoked.
A claim then exempts the row from every sweep.
sweeps.scale:
Measured:
- 4,533 public listings are eligible for instant claim.
- 1,150 of them have a dead site. RDAP showed 14 of 20 sampled dns_fail .com roots are unregistered, so an estimated 290-560 roots (about 480 listings) can be bought today.
- gulfportcigars.com was re-registered on 2026-08-17.
- 314 eligible working links redirect to another domain.
- 12 listings sit on public-suffix, free-mail or government hosts.
- 1,662 listings share 420 domains.
- 13,850 verdict-hidden rows can be claimed.
No harm yet: 0 claims exist and SMTP is off.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Accept that about two-thirds of claims (2,996 of 4,533 on today's data) go to staff review. SMTP credentials. Decide what proof staff accept for manual claims, such as a call-back to the listed phone.
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: Real owners with a down, shared or new site wait for staff. The gate never rejects a claim; it only removes the self-serve shortcut. Test that all 25 live examples from the audit behave as expected (the 12 bad suffixes, the 4 dead domains and the 14 gambling redirects are refused; the 5 good domains pass).
sweeps.effort: About 2.5 days (gate 1.5, staff review changes 1)

sweeps.name: Menu scanner: unstick the queue, expire stale stock, attach shared feeds to the right branch
sweeps.problem: scanStale re-reads the same 323 failed or unsupported shops every 6 hours, because a failed read never records the matcher version. As a result no new shop is ever read, and most current shelves will stop refreshing while their 'in stock' claims stay up indefinitely. #875 fails every scan, yet its rows stay in stock. Meanwhile, one online store's stock appears at every listing sharing its website: 3J's feed (the site presents only Lake Worth) shows at 4 listings, including '1804 Cigars Davie', which the site never names.
sweeps.scale: Measured by replay: in the next 30 days, 36 of 43 public shelves get no re-read and 0 never-read listings are reached. 11 public listings on 4 websites share a feed (7 extra copies). The latent exposure is 1,449 unread public listings that share a website with another listing.
sweeps.method:
1) scanStale: record an attempt stamp on every outcome. Back off by outcome: ok 7 days, unsupported 60, errors 3, 7, 14, then 30. Skip dead website statuses. Put never-read listings ahead of low-value re-reads.
2) Expiry: when a shop's last successful read is older than N days, set its web rows to in_stock=0 with an 'expired' marker. Turn the 'checked N days ago' label amber after 7 days.
3) Shared websites: attach the feed only to the listing whose address the site names. The others get 'This company sells online at <site>', and listings the site never names get nothing. Decide the chain rule (Anthony's x3).
4) A first write for a never-read shop requires the name check, an unshared host, storefront='yes' and not closed.
The widening crawl itself is rank 31; the critic says to sample 50 unread sites across confidence bands before sizing its yield.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: The expiry window (14, 21 or 30 days) and how a chain's single web store shows at its branches.
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: A shop whose site blocks us for 3 weeks loses a real shelf. That is honest, since we can no longer vouch for it. Only 4 shared-feed groups exist today, all reviewed by hand.
sweeps.effort: About 1 day

sweeps.name: Search that finds what people type: apostrophes, aliases, city plus state, local autocomplete
sweeps.problem: Store search is a plain ILIKE with no punctuation folding. 'wild bills' finds 2 of 215 Wild Bill's listings, 'smokin joes' 0 of 18, and 'holts' 0 of 3. City chips match substrings in every state: the Jacksonville chip mixes in 13 North Carolina shops, and 'Washington, DC' returns rows from MI, MO and PA. Navbar autocomplete ignores location, so typing 'cigar' offers the three Tucson Anthony's to everyone.
sweeps.scale: Measured: 926 public names contain an apostrophe. 22 of the top 40 city chips mix in other towns (121 rows); 19 of them mix in other states (82 rows).
sweeps.method:
1) Add a name_search column maintained from name plus aliases (former names from ranks 11 and 17): lower-case, strip apostrophes and periods, fold accents, and treat '&' as 'and'. Fold St/Saint and Mt/Mount for cities.
2) Chips send city and state, matched exactly. A typed city resolves to a centre and runs rank 12 with a 15-mi radius.
3) Apply the same fix to the city LIKE in cigars.js.
4) Autocomplete passes the saved location, ordered by match quality and then distance.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: This affects search only. Guardrail: every chip's result count must equal the chip's own count.
sweeps.effort: Half to 1 day

sweeps.name: Same-door duplicate merge, and stop the build from re-creating duplicates
sweeps.problem: The same shop appears two or three times at one door, and the copies disagree: one shows hours and 'Open now', the other doesn't; one has the Lounge badge, the other doesn't. Examples: The Pipe Rack / 'The Pipe' in Akron; three Roz's Cigar Emporium rows in Ocala; Wild Bill's Berkley ('Twelve Mile' vs '12 Mile'). dedupeListings finds 0 more, because its exact-name, same-city rule is too narrow. osm.namesMatch fails on 'Cole's' vs 'Coles' and 'JR Cigars - Clayton' vs 'JR Cigars'. The importer never retires a row the rebuilt file folded away.
sweeps.scale: Measured: 148 public listings in 73 clusters, 75 extra rows, all hand-checked; 3 are wrong, so about 72 true extras. 41 of the extras are OSM rows. 35 twin pairs have pins more than 300 m apart, and rank 9 settles which pin is right. The location auditor found 55 address-less OSM pins within 150 m of an addressed listing, which are probable duplicates.
sweeps.method:
1) Same door: same house number plus at least 50% of street words shared after normalising (Twelve to 12, SR/State Rd/US to 'hwy N', suites removed), with the same ZIP or city; or pins within 60 m.
2) Same shop: names equal after folding punctuation and plurals, or distinctive words match with trade words and the town name removed.
3) Merge automatically only with a matching phone or website host, or when one twin is a bare record. Different house numbers, conflicting phones and clusters of 3+ go to review.
4) Survivor: the row holding inventory or activity, then the pin agreeing with the geocode, then the working website, then website hours. Fill its empty fields from the twin. Hide the rest with storefront='duplicate' and a pointer, and re-point child rows.
5) Fix osm.js nameKey (apostrophes, '&', joined initials, squashed spaces, drop the town word). Let buildDirectory fold every OSM twin, not only the first. Have importStores hide an existing OSM row that the new file folded into an Overture record.
6) Run the automatic tier after every import.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: One decision: a shop and its in-house lounge on one phone (JR Cigar + Casa de Montecristo x3, House of Cigar + HOC D.Ellan): one listing or two?
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: The risk is merging neighbours. Bellevue Cigar at 565 Lincoln and a separate dealer at 553 matched only on the town name. Guardrails: the town name never counts toward a match; hide, never delete; review the whole dry run (about 80 rows); matcher self-tests with negatives (Holt's/Ashton, Tobacco Town/Tobacco Row).
sweeps.effort: About 1 day build, 2 h review

sweeps.name: Current name at the door: stale former names and rebrands
sweeps.problem:
A former business name is still listed next to the current one, or instead of it. Examples:
- 13989 S Dixie Hwy (Pinecrest) is listed as Top Notch, Vilar and Miami Humidor; only Miami Humidor is current.
- Hill Country Humidor now serves a betting site; the shop there is The Cigar Vault.
- Almonte Tobacconist is listed beside Don Francisco Cigars Too.
- Carrot Top Corporation is really Cigaret Shopper.
- JO Cigars Cape Coral is really Habanos's Smoke Shop.
The closure sweep can't catch these, because the phone still works.
sweeps.scale: Measured: 94 same-door clusters, 95 extra rows. All 6 checked were stale, so the estimate is 55-75. Licences add 24 replaced-name candidates (4 of 4 checked renamed; overlaps rank 11). About 12 more are suspected rebrands from redirects (seriouscigars.com to casademontecristo.com, birminghamcigars.com to vitolafinecigars.com). Cheap Tobacco and Northern Michigan Tobacco belong to rank 18.
sweeps.method:
For each cluster, gather: chain locator feeds naming the street; JSON-LD name, address and title on each twin's working site; site health (placeholder or hijacked pages, from rank 7); Overture status; the active licence DBA once rank 11 exists; and which twin holds inventory.
Hide a twin as a duplicate only when a working source names the current business at this street, the twin's name appears nowhere on it, and the twin's own site is dead, a placeholder or absent. Keep both when each has its own working site and phone. A single listing whose licence or locator names a different current business gets a proposed rename, with the old name kept as an alias.
Write a decisions file; nothing is applied automatically.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Same decision as rank 16 on shop plus in-house lounge.
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: The risk is hiding a live second venue, or keeping the stale name as the survivor. Guardrails: the survivor needs positive evidence; different phones plus different working sites means keep both (Holt's and Ashton upstairs); review every decision; hide, never delete. Renames need rank 1.
sweeps.effort: 1 day build, 2 h review

sweeps.name: Chain reconcile from the chains' own store locators, including missing branches
sweeps.problem:
Three kinds of chain errors:
- Rebranded branches still carry the old name, no hours and a link to an acquisition notice. Cheap Tobacco Wooster (#18924) is Wild Bill's of Wooster at the same address and phone; Northern Michigan Tobacco Gladwin is now Sweet Fire.
- The same branch appears twice (Riverview, Napoleon, Eastpointe).
- Some branches are missing entirely: Wild Bill's Findlay (Tiffin Ave), Sweet Fire Tomah, Marquette x2 and Mondovi.
Also, 37 confirmed branches show no hours because of 'Twp' vs town and '13 Mile' vs 'Thirteen Mile' mismatches. 17 of Wild Bill's 19 lounge branches lack the Lounge badge. #41184 'Wild Bill's Tobacco (Coming Soon)' is a stub with no store behind it.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: The display name (brand, or the per-store name like 'Wild Bill's of Wooster'). Scope: are tobacco and vape chains in a cigar finder (about 310 public already; this adds 48)?
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: The risk is renaming a different business in the same plaza (Every Day Tobacco, Ste 2). Guardrails: a rename needs a phone match; absence never hides a row (Wild Bill's says 250+ stores while its locator lists 237); review all 48 inserts on a map. Needs rank 1.
sweeps.effort: About 1.5 days build, 3-4 h review

sweeps.name: Wrong-site and platform links
sweeps.problem: Many links shown as a shop's Website are someone else's site: Groveside Tobacco links Rube's Steaks; others link azlyrics.com, rentacenter.com, atf.gov and tigers.com. Some belong to a different business entirely: Tobacco Master links a grout company, Arizona Tobacco a trellis maker, Dream Tobacco a dream-meaning site, and these supply thumbnails too. 247 links are social, directory, Google, event, job or payment pages, such as an Eventbrite ticket page for Puro Cigar Bar or plus.google.com, and bare twitter.com and yelp.com roots. OSM often has the real site (purocigarbar.com, papscigarco.com). 69 dead deep links hide a working root domain (JO Cigars /index.html).
sweeps.scale: Measured: 432 public listings the hours sweep found 'never names this shop' are all still shown as links. A 60-row desk review found 29 wrong, 14 right and 17 unclear, which extrapolates to about 210-330. 116 more have unrelated domains (about 86 wrong). 11 wrong-business thumbnails. 247 platform links. 61 OSM twins give a different website. 21 deep links have a working root (10-15 recoverable).
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Keep social profiles as labelled links (recommended)? Show Overture's Facebook page for listings with no working site (up to 2,358)?
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: The risk is failing a real shop whose name appears only in its logo. Guardrails: logo alt text and og:site_name count, any phone or address match passes, and every fail is reviewed (the desk sample shows about 14 in 60 flagged are right). Only links change, never the shop.
sweeps.effort: 1.5-2 days build, 3-4 h review

sweeps.name: Phone corrections
sweeps.problem: Some Call buttons ring the wrong number. Sunset Cigar Lounge shows (725) 240-1932 while its site prints 204-1932. Placeholders appear: (999) 999-9999 on Mobtown, 555-5555 twice. One chain-wide number is on 11 Tobacco Hut doors across three states, although OSM carries local numbers for 4 of them. Jm Cigar Bar in Puerto Rico carries an Illinois shop's phone. Importer line 112 overwrites every phone, including corrected ones.
sweeps.method:
Add phone_source (via rank 1).
E1: clear placeholder and non-US numbers.
E4: for shared chain lines, use the OSM twin's number or the chain store page's number where one exists; otherwise keep the chain number. For different-business pairs, the listing whose own site shows the number keeps it.
E5: on single-location sites that pass the identity check, read only JSON-LD telephone and tel: links, ignoring fax, text and events numbers. Propose a replacement only when the site shows exactly one number and ours appears nowhere on it. Review every replacement.
JS-drawn sites (Cig's & Gar's) need the headless render.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Nothing for the free checks. Optionally about $55 once (Twilio Lookup) to find numbers that are no longer in service.
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: The risk is a fax or second-location number replacing the right one (the Tinder Box Dublin false alarm). Guardrails: the tel:/markup-only and single-number rules, never overwrite owner phones, review everything.
sweeps.effort: About 1 day plus 2-3 h review

sweeps.name: Owner and staff edits: log, re-check, and no invented hours
sweeps.problem: The owner edit route rewrites name, address, state, phone and website with no geocode, no time-zone or link re-check, and no log. A new website keeps the old dead status or the old redirect target, so it stays hidden, or visitors are sent to the old hijacked destination. The settings form pre-fills template hours, and saving any field publishes them with hours_source='owner', which locks out every sweep. The template matches only 5.2% of known day values. Claimed rows stop receiving any closure evidence. Staff have no phone or website editor, and the Links queue lists only dead statuses.
sweeps.scale: Dormant: 0 claims today. Would hit the 6,120 public listings with unknown hours on first save, the 1,323 whose unclaimed banner promises a link fix, and about 371 listings with a stale redirect target.
sweeps.method:
1) PUT diffs against the row and writes store_edits (rank 1). hours_source='owner' is set only when the hours actually changed, with no template pre-fill.
2) A website change nulls the status and final URL and calls linkCheck.checkStore right away.
3) An address change re-geocodes and recomputes the timezone. A move of more than 2 km, a new state, an unrelated name or a new area code waits for staff, and the old values stay live meanwhile.
4) Owner-created listings are geocoded and deduped against rows within 150 m.
5) Staff get a phone and website editor that writes a source, not staff_edited. The Links queue adds the new verdicts.
6) Claimed rows still record source closures and closureCheck flags. Visitor 'closed' reports go to the queue and email the owner. Claimed rows are never auto-hidden.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Which owner fields go live instantly and which wait for staff. Proposed: hours, phone and website go live, with re-checks.
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: Staging slows real rebrands, so only large changes are staged, and staff see before and after side by side.
sweeps.effort: 1.5-2 days

sweeps.name: Profile honesty quick fixes
sweeps.problem:
Unclaimed profiles promise things that never happen.
- The Request tile on every profile opens nothing, and requests could only be read by an owner, of which there are none.
- The claim modal promises an email that never sends while SMTP is off.
- The banner credits OpenStreetMap on listings that are 93% Overture.
- The unclaimed banner prints the dead domain.
- It says inventory appears only once claimed, on 43 listings that already show inventory.
sweeps.scale: Measured: 7,431 profiles show a dead button. 6,887 carry the wrong data credit. 1,323 name a dead domain. 43 have the wrong inventory line.
sweeps.method:
- Hide the Request tile unless the listing is claimed, or build it as outreach.
- Refuse inventory requests on hidden stores.
- Change 'we'll email you' to 'check back here' while SMTP is unset, and add a pending-claims badge in the admin nav.
- Credit 'Overture Maps Foundation and OpenStreetMap contributors'.
- Stop printing dead domains.
- Show the 'appears once claimed' line only when no web menu exists.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Collect requests on unclaimed listings for outreach, or just hide the tile?
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: None to data.
sweeps.effort: About 2 h

sweeps.name: Server-side map clustering
sweeps.problem: The map viewport query caps at 1,000 rows and clusters in the browser. Views wider than a large state drop pins, and cluster counts understate density by up to 7x. At national zoom Michigan shows 7 pins for 447 listings, and SD, ND and VT show none. The pricing page tells owners to 'find your shop on the map'.
sweeps.scale: Measured, live: the national view represents 1,000 of 7,417 listings. 6 of 15 measured viewports are capped. Each pan downloads 1.34 MB.
sweeps.method: Add GET /stores/map?bbox&zoom&filters that groups by the same grid cell formula as the client. Return individual pins only for single-row cells or at zoom 12 and above, plus an exact total. Test that cluster counts sum to COUNT(*) in the bbox for the 15 viewports in m5.js.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: Display only. Keep the client's cell formula so the look doesn't change.
sweeps.effort: About 1 day

sweeps.name: Neutral order when no location is known
sweeps.problem: With no location, the list sorts by web-feed size and then alphabetically, so every visitor's Home 'Local Retailers' shows three identical Tucson Anthony's feeds and Florida online-first sellers. The review-form store picker offers only those same 300 shops, so a Michigan smoker can pick 3 of 447. 68 of the 300 have a dead site or a likely_closed flag.
sweeps.scale: Measured: 7,131 of 7,431 public listings (96%) never appear without a place or name search.
sweeps.method:
- Drop inventory_count and follower_count as global sort keys.
- With no location, order by completeness (working site, hours, phone, thumbnail), demote likely-closed and dead-site rows, and shuffle daily. Show one listing per website host or feed per page.
- Home uses the saved location to show the nearest 6, or retitles itself.
- The review picker becomes a type-ahead.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: What a visitor with no location sees: a prompt, a national sample, or IP geolocation (MaxMind GeoLite2 needs a free licence key). Also how paid placement appears in no-location views.
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: Order only, no data changes. Snapshot tests check that no host repeats on page 1 and that page 1 spans at least 10 states.
sweeps.effort: About 1 day

sweeps.name: Recover real cigar shops that are hidden or missing (size it first)
sweeps.problem:
Some real cigar lounges are hidden or missing:
- Hidden by the name classifier because Overture miscategorised them as e-cigarette stores: Casa de Montecristo West Loop in Houston, Capital Cigar Lincoln.
- Hidden because the regex doesn't know the word: Harry's Habana Hut, Cigarz Lounge.
- Marked not_retail because '<Town> Cigars' lacks a premises word.
- Missing from the directory entirely: BURN by Rocky Patel in Naples, Stony Brook Tobacconist, Jernigan's in Mt. Lebanon, Cheroots Cypress. These show up in licence registries, and some lounges have no 'cigar' in their name (Club Macanudo).
Hidden rows have never been link-, closure- or hours-checked. Annapolis Cigar Co is closed and Capital Cigar's address is stale.
sweeps.method:
1) Apply the classifier vocabulary fixes from rank 8, in the direction of making rows public: havana, habana, maduro, robusto, vitola, churchill, tabac*, cigar[a-z]+. An alternate e_cigarette_store category stops setting shop=e-cigarette.
2) Run linkCheck, closureCheck and the hours collect over the candidate pool.
3) Accept a row when:
- a working site names the shop and shows cigar evidence (humidor, brand list, 'cigar lounge'); or
- it has a phone, Overture confidence of at least 0.9, a meta or Foursquare source, and no public twin within 150 m; or
- it holds an active licence plus a second storefront source.
4) Reject on closure text, a dead domain with no phone, a brand or factory page with no address, or an Overture closed flag.
5) Write storefront='yes' with the reason 'rescued: <evidence>'. Licence-only shops are inserted hidden for staff.
6) Extend the Overture extract to bars and lounges whose name or site carries cigar vocabulary or brand names.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: May staff publish a listing whose only sources are a licence plus Overture or OSM?
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: The risk is publishing closed or moved shops, or vape shops licensed under a 'cigar' company name (V&A Cigar Corp). Guardrails: live corroboration, address updates only from the site's structured data, and human review of every row without a website.
sweeps.effort: Half a day to sample, then 2 days build and about 1 day review

sweeps.name: Hours recovery from evidence already on disk
sweeps.problem: Plainly stated hours were refused. Examples: Central Cigars in St Petersburg has a clean address-tied table, recorded as 'no hours found'. Cigaret Shopper tables lost their day labels. Chain branches lost hours over 'Brownstown Twp' vs 'Brownstown' (rank 18 covers Wild Bill's and Sweet Fire).
sweeps.scale: Measured: 405 listings with no hours have a readable 3-day, 3-time block on a captured page. 18 of the 99 'no hours found' cases parse cleanly today. Estimate: 60-150 listings gain hours.
sweeps.method: Re-run decide over the saved evidence with parser fixes: split column tables, 'Store'-prefixed lines, '&' day lists, misspelled days, 'Closed all other days'. Accept only blocks tied to the listing's street, ZIP or phone, covering 5 or more days with no conflicts, and pass them through the rank 6 guards. Review, then apply.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: The risk is a wrong-branch match on chain pages. Guardrails: require an address tie, refuse blocks with another town between the address and the hours, and apply only a reviewed file.
sweeps.effort: 1 day build, 2-3 h review

sweeps.name: Full-page website read: lounge badge, walk-in humidor, members-only, brands carried, logos
sweeps.problem: The Lounge badge is set from Overture's cigar_bar category even with nothing else to support it: a mobile event service, an online store, a cigar roller and a price-comparison site all carry it. Real lounges lack it, including shops whose own hours are 'Lounge Hours' (Nicahabana, Aficionado's, GarVino's). 'Walk-in Humidor' is only the word 'humidor' in the name, so it tags online humidor sellers and misses real walk-ins (Creekside, Little Havana). Members-only lounges look public (The Boardroom, Hogshead). No brand list is stored anywhere, although the owner wants one. Schema.org logos (924) are unused.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Decide whether 'not confirmed' means no badge (recommended), whether to show a 'Members only' qualifier, which amenity chips to show, and the brand-list wording.
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: The risks are a sister branch's lounge credited to every branch, and blog or FAQ text. Guardrails: branch binding and disqualifiers, 2 review rounds of about 60 decisions, and never hide a listing.
sweeps.effort: 2-2.5 days build, about 1.5 h crawl, 4 h review

sweeps.name: Scope decision, then precision review of the weak public bands
sweeps.problem: Being public is decided by a name test. A 'Tobacco' or 'Pipe' name scores 0.55 and is public; a neutral name scores 0.45 and is hidden. So the same chain is public in one town and hidden in the next: Smoker Friendly has 2 public and 119 hidden; 'Tobacco Barn' is public while 'Tobacco Outlet' is hidden.
sweeps.scale: 3,001 public band-D ('Tobacco' or 'Pipe' only) listings. A desk sample of 60 found about 15% not cigar places (95% CI about 8-26%, roughly 450 listings; an estimate). 693 hidden branches sit on 147 domains that also have public branches.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: The product scope decision.
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: The risk is hiding a general tobacco shop that does keep a humidor. Guardrails: never auto-hide a row with any cigar evidence, queue rather than hide, and review per chain.
sweeps.effort: A decision, then about 1.5 days and 3-4 h review

sweeps.name: Text cleanup: names, cities, ZIPs and addresses
sweeps.problem: Names and addresses carry clutter from the sources. Names: trailing 'LLC', ALL CAPS 'TOBACCO HUT', internal store numbers ('Low Bob's Tobacco #1050'), and marketing tails ('Voted Best Bar in NKY 2025 & 2024', '20% off Cigars!'). 255 names are only a category ('Tobacco Shop' x39). Cities: our own titleCase gives 'Winston-salem' and 'Mcallen'; OSM gives county names ('Cobb County'); USPS gives abbreviations ('Wshngtn Ct Hs'). Addresses: 'TBD', 'If You Don't Know You Can't Come!', and landmark prefixes ('Behind Outback Steakhouse').
sweeps.scale: Measured: about 290 cosmetic name fixes, about 37 marketing or status names, 255 category-only names (30-60 recoverable from sites), about 260 city fixes, 266 missing ZIPs, and about 290 address strings.
sweeps.method:
- tidyName at import from source_name: trailing legal words only, repair casing artifacts, strip 3+ digit store numbers only when shared by a chain, and re-case only all-upper or all-lower names, using the site's own spelling or a reviewer.
- Marketing tails cut at a separator when followed by marketing or product words. Status words are routed: Coming Soon to closure, No Public Sales to not_retail, members-only to a note, 'formerly X' to an alias.
- Category-only names take og:site_name or JSON-LD name only when the page shows our address or phone.
- Fix titleCase for Mc, Mac, O' and hyphens.
- Cities: expand USPS abbreviations, and replace county names with the postal city of the ZIP.
- Fill ZIPs from the ZCTA containing the pin.
- Blank non-addresses, and move landmark prefixes into a note.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Township display: the postal city ('Utica') or the legal name ('Shelby Twp')? Keep chains' public #1-#14 branch numbers (recommended)?
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: The risk is mangling a stylised brand. Guardrails: never touch mixed-case names, every case change is reviewed, everything is reversible from source_name, and owner rows are untouched. Needs rank 1.
sweeps.effort: 1.5 days build, 1 h review

sweeps.name: Thumbnail vetting and re-hosting
sweeps.scale: Measured: at least 126 of 1,427 thumbnails are wrong, unsuitable or unusable. 50 near-blank logos. 232 branch photos repeated on other branches, plus 93 cropped banners. 32 fail to load (the monogram fallback works). 86 are over 1 MB.
sweeps.method:
thumbCheck job:
- Fetch each image and record size, pixels and a perceptual hash, and render it the way the card does.
- Drop images under 120 px, deny-listed URLs (builder defaults, theme demos, stock paths, favicons, marketplaces), the same hash on 2 or more unrelated domains, and images blank on both backgrounds.
- Store web_image_bg when the other background works.
- Apply the chain policy to repeated non-logo images.
- Then cache approved images as 160 px WebP on our own storage, re-checked monthly.
- Fill gaps from schema.org logos already collected.
- Add an owner upload for logo and cover, and a staff 'remove picture' action.
Review contact sheets before applying.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: The chain policy (chain logo, monogram, or keep the banner), and approval to re-host share images (R2 keys, or about 10 MB in Postgres).
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: A false drop only returns a shop to its monogram. Soft signals go to review.
sweeps.effort: About 2 days total, plus 1 h contact-sheet review

sweeps.name: Complete and widen the stock readers, plus shelf hygiene
sweeps.problem:
The stock readers miss a lot, and some shelves show junk.
- WooCommerce: the brand is dropped and reads stop at 800 products. Lake Worth Cigars has 1,504 products and matches 39.
- A 2 MB body cap breaks #875.
- BigCommerce, Wix and Squarespace shops are skipped. Corona Cigar has 3,371 products with brand and availability microdata.
- Coffee and travel cases appear as cigars.
- Some brands are really vendor phrases ('Rolled in Ybor city with Cuban technique').
- One shop's typo reads $187,699.
sweeps.scale: Measured: WooCommerce matches 61% of cigar products vs Shopify's 92% (20 shops). 208 public listings are 'unsupported'. 24 non-cigar lines, about 103 mislabeled lines and 1 absurd price on public shelves. The critic says the scanner's 160-shelf widening estimate is inflated: sample 50 unread sites across confidence bands first.
sweeps.method:
- WooCommerce: take the brand from the brands field, a pa_brand attribute, or a category equal to an established brand; paginate by X-WP-TotalPages; raise the cap to 8 MB for JSON.
- Shopify: paginate until an empty page.
- Read BigCommerce product sitemaps and microdata, Wix store sitemaps plus JSON-LD, and Squarespace ?format=json, at 1.5 s per page, 600 pages per run, stopping on 403 or 429.
- Extend NOT_CIGAR (coffee, caddy, telescopic, scissors) with a size-token exception.
- Retire non-brand lines, and fold misspelled brands through a reviewed list.
- Price guard per stick using the pack count.
- Re-run the matcher offline on cached feeds first; Shopify results must not change.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Approve crawling up to a few thousand product pages per shop.
sweeps.risk_and_guardrail: The risk is a category mistaken for a brand. Guardrails: the established-brand rule, and review 50 new matches before applying.
sweeps.effort: About 2.5 days

sweeps.name: Visitor feedback prompts: hours, closed, lounge

plan.solid:
Already done well, so these do not need a new sweep:
- **Pins.** The median pin is 56 m from the shop's own address, 97.7% are within 1 km, and none are snapped to city centres. Every public row has a pin, state, city and time zone.
- **Time zones.** They are right for 99.6% of listings. Daylight saving works through IANA zones, and Arizona, Hawaii and Puerto Rico are correct.
- **The core of the directory.** The 4,008 cigar-named public listings are about 95% genuine. A 44-shop probe of famous names (Davidoff, Smoke Inn, Two Guys, Iwan Ries and others) found nearly all of them present and public.
- **Chain hours.** Hours on matched chain branches agree with the chains' own feeds in 221 of 222 cases.
- **The website hours sweep.** 146 of 150 reviewed decisions were right, no template defaults repeat across unrelated sites, and every stored hours value parses.
- **linkCheck's dead-link handling.** 1,323 dead links are hidden, including the 166 retired business.site pages. 403/429 responses count as working, and re-checks run every 12 hours.
- **Existing verdicts.** storefrontCheck's 537 non-retail hides, dedupeListings' 34 duplicates and chainCheck's 7 closed branches are right and are honoured on re-import. chainCheck's conservative holdbacks were mostly correct.
- **Overture closures.** Its permanently_closed flag is mostly right (2 of 3 sampled). The no-contact rule correctly only flags and never hides. Visitor reports need 2 independent votes.
- **Claim security basics.** Codes are hashed, expire, and are rate-limited. Claimed and staff-edited rows are consistently protected from sweeps.
- **The client.** StoreThumb falls back to the monogram on every failed image, and no-referrer rescues 5 listings. openStatus never shows unknown hours as Closed.
- **Store pages and stock.** The store page and 'Where to find it' filter to visible stores and hide $0 prices. Stock prices are plausible (1 bad price in 12,306 sizes), and every shelf is fresh today.

Do not redo two ideas from the worklog. Treating 'dead website plus no phone' as a closure is wrong: 11 of 11 sampled dead-site shops were open. The '$200 Google credit' plan is out of date.
plan.ongoing:
Recurring jobs and checks, most of which already exist or are proposed in the sweeps above.

**Every import or deploy:**
- Run the re-import test (rank 1).
- Run the same-door duplicate auto-tier.
- Every job writes to the edit log.

**Every 12 hours:**
- Keep linkCheck, now with the identity verdicts (elsewhere, hijacked, parked, store unavailable).
- On any owner or staff website edit, re-check that site immediately.

**Every 6 hours:**
- Run the menu scanner with outcome back-off.
- Expire stock that has not been read successfully for 21 days.

**Weekly:**
- Re-read the website hours of lounges, of listings with views or follows, and of the 19 seasonal schedules.
- Run extra passes after Labor Day, Oct 1 and Memorial Day.

**Monthly:**
- **Hours:** re-collect every website-sourced listing (about 25 minutes). Auto-apply only when the new reading matches the stored one or two runs agree; any change goes to review.
- **Overture:** refresh with a change diff. An id dropped from two releases goes to the closure queue.
- **Licence registries:** re-sync. TX, FL, PA and Chicago publish daily if wanted.
- **Chains:** re-pull the chain locator feeds. A branch missing from two pulls goes to review.
- **Thumbnails:** re-check them by hash.
- **Registrations:** run an RDAP pass on dead and redirected domains, which feeds the claim guard.

**Nightly or in CI:**
- The recall monitor replays 62 metros x 4 radii x filters and 15 map viewports against a brute-force truth set, and fails below 100%.
- Compute a claim_proof verdict for every public listing.

**Around holidays:** on Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day, show 'Holiday, hours may differ' instead of the green badge, unless the site says it opens on holidays.

**Staff, about 1-2 hours a week:** clear the Closures, Links, Claims and Listings queues, sorted by strength of evidence. A person approves every hide, rename and move. Nothing a single signal flags is auto-hidden.

missing_areas.focus:
Audit the ownership channel. Once a listing is claimed it overrides every sweep. Instant claim (utils/claims.js emailMatchesWebsite) trusts the domain of the listing's stored website. It never checks website_status, where the site redirects, or when the domain was registered.

Measured on the public snapshot:
- 4,533 of 4,863 websites qualify for instant email verification. 1,150 of those are dead, 756 of them dns_fail.
- Verisign RDAP on 12 seeded-random dns_fail .com domains: 8 are unregistered, so anyone can buy them (tobaccokingia.com #13278, roosevelttobacco.com #15724, ortegasmokeshop.com #6162). gulfportcigars.com (#278) was re-registered on 2026-08-17.
- 314 qualifying working links redirect to a different registrable domain.
- rootDomain() keeps only the last two labels. Any @yahoo.com mailbox passes for #3889, #15090, #20502 and #26628 (local.yahoo.com pages) and #21932 (yahoo.com). Any .com.au or .co.uk mailbox passes for #640, #3624 and #12092. Any *.tx.us mailbox passes for #2445 (dars.state.tx.us).
- 420 domains are shared by 1,662 listings (wildbillstobacco.com alone has 203), so staff at one branch can claim the others.

This is dormant only because SMTP is not configured yet (WORKLOG).

What a claim unlocks:
- The row is exempt from the importer, from closure reports and from every proposed sweep.
- PUT /stores/:id rewrites name, address, state, phone and website with no geocode, time-zone or link re-check, and nothing is logged.
- Staff approval (approveClaim with verify=true) sets visible=1 even on rows marked storefront closed or duplicate.

Also check what unclaimed listings promise. The Request tile on every profile sets a modal state that is never rendered, so the button does nothing. POST inventory-requests stores rows that only an owner can read, and no listing has an owner.

Sweep and guard ideas:
- Require website_status ok and the same registrable domain after redirects.
- Require an RDAP creation date older than the directory record.
- Use a real public-suffix list, and block free-mail and .gov/.us hosts.
- Send chain domains to staff review.
- Keep closure evidence flowing to review for claimed rows.
- Log every owner edit with its before and after values.

Use public tobacco-retailer license registries as an independent second source for whether a shop exists, whether it closed, its address, its trading name, and which shops are missing. ROADMAP.md names them as the validation layer; no auditor used one.

Measured for New York City only. Source: the city's 'Legally Operating Businesses' dataset, Tobacco Retail Dealer category, on its free open-data API. It has 6,707 records with status, expiry, phone, address and lat/lng. Script: work/meta/nycmatch.js.
- Of 111 public NYC listings, 61 match a license by phone, or by house number plus ZIP plus a shared street word.
- 48 of those match an Active license. 13 match only inactive licenses (Expired, Surrendered, Revoked or Suspended).

Checked 3 of the 13:
- #21243 Davidoff of Geneva, Brookfield Place: license expired 2025-12-31. The store has closed (halfwheel; Yelp 'CLOSED - Updated July 2026') and is still public.
- #22132 Amadiz Cigars: license expired 2024, but Yelp shows it trading in May 2026. A lapsed license is a signal, not proof.
- #21732 Cigar Inn: unresolved.

Other findings:
- #21203 Mulberry Street Cigars: the Active license carrying our phone number is at 140 Mulberry St, while we list 176. That is a second source for the location auditor's move candidate.
- 3 active cigar licensees have no row anywhere in the 42,923: Grand Havana Room (666 5th Ave), Bay Cigars and Tobacco (1201 Bay St), Three 1862 Cigars (593 Washington Ave).

To do:
- List which cities and states publish free bulk files. NYC is verified. One search found only an application form for Florida's DBPR permits, no bulk list; check Chicago, TX, CA, NJ and MD.
- Join listings by phone and address.
- Send 'no active license' to the closure queue only together with a second signal.
- Use licensed trading names (DBA) for rename review and licensed addresses for move review.
- Count active cigar and tobacconist licensees that are missing from the directory.

Guard against:
- corporate names that differ from the sign;
- a convenience-store license at a shared door (#21052 Cigar Palace matched only a deli's expired license at 268 Kings Hwy);
- registry lag.

Check which listings a customer is actually shown for a place and a filter, not only whether each row is correct. GET /stores (routes/stores.js) sorts by is_featured, claimed, verified, follower_count, inventory_count, confidence, name. It then applies LIMIT (300 by default, and the list page sends no limit). Only after that does it sort by distance and apply the open_now filter in JavaScript.

Measured on the snapshot:
- With the default 50-mile radius around Midtown Manhattan, the query box holds 410 public listings. The list keeps 300 by confidence, which drops about 20 of the 64 listings within 5 miles (e.g. #41493 Manhattan Tobacco at 0.7 mi, #21257 333 Smoke Shop at 1.2 mi).
- LA (301 in radius) and Miami (299 in the box) sit at the cap. The relevance rescue and chain additions would push them over.
- 'Open now' filters only the 300 rows already kept.
- The map viewport query caps at 1,000 rows, so any view wider than one large state drops pins and undercounts clusters.
- The nationwide list with no location opens with Anthony's three identical feed copies (#2063, #2076, #2134), then the online-first sellers Cigar Boulevard, Cigars Direct and GT Cigars. That happens because inventory_count is the first sort key that is non-zero today.

What to do:
- Measure, per metro and per filter, what share of the true in-radius matches is returned.
- Order by distance and apply filters in SQL, or use a hard radius with no silent cap.
- Cluster the map server-side.
- Use a default order that does not reward feed size or duplicated feeds.

All figures come from node scripts run over the 2026-09-10 snapshot. The scripts are in C:/Users/mason/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Users-mason-OneDrive-Desktop-cigarApp/a956c8ab-bec6-4085-b83b-7fcd97853bc4/scratchpad/audit/work/closures/ (m1.js, m2.js, m3.js, reloc.js, reloc2.js, reloc_ev.js, closedtwin.js, redir.js, osmfetch.js).

PUBLIC (7,431 listings)
- operating_status: open 5,649, null 1,737, likely_closed 45. No claimed listings; 2 are staff_edited.
- Dead website (status dns_fail/not_found/parked/refused/timeout/error): 1,323. By status: dns_fail 756, not_found 330, error 71, refused 60, timeout 58, parked 48.
  - 1,278 of the 1,323 have a phone. The 45 without a phone are exactly the 45 likely_closed rows.

HIDDEN (full 42,923 listings)
- 564 are operating_status permanently_closed: 560 from Overture and 4 from the website signal.

FRESHNESS
