problems.title: A dead website does not mean a closed shop: the 1,323 dead-link listings are mostly trading
problems.affected_public: 1,323 public listings with a dead site, 1,278 of them with a phone. 11 sampled: 0 closed and 11 open, so the closed share is probably under 24% (95% upper bound) and likely much lower. 166 of the links are retired Google business.site pages, 84 are broken deep paths on a live domain, and some 'error' results are false: cigarsonmainnj.com answers 200 today.
problems.how_measured: Seeded stratified random sample (sample.js), each checked by web search or fetch, plus a re-fetch of the sites with 'error' or 'timeout' status.
examples: #20328 Greenville Cigar Lounge, Wilmington DE: dns_fail (the domain no longer resolves), but Yelp was updated July 2026 and the shop is trading. Our phone (302) 579-8259 differs from the 302-562-8402 on its web listings.
#8797 Cigar Loft, Walnut Creek: dns_fail. Yelp updated Feb 2026, active Facebook. Open.
#868 Smoke & Barrel, Miami: our link smokeandbarrellounge.com/new-home is not_found, but the root site answers 200. Open.
#21070 Cigars on Main, Freehold NJ: status 'error', yet the site answers 200 today. Open.

#9166 Vintage Havana, Ridgecrest (parked), #10807 A Little Bit of Big Sky, Kalispell (not_found), #19163 Trial & Error, Bridgeville (not_found), #1233 River City Cigars (dns_fail), #3605 Handmade Casillas (dns_fail), #15320 Tobacco Marketplace (dns_fail), #5907 Black Dog Cigar (dns_fail): all open per Yelp, Facebook or BBB.
problems.customer_impact: No harm today, because the site link is already hidden. But a sweep that treats a dead site as a closure would pull about 1,200 real shops off the map. That rules out the 'dead website' shortcut the worklog suggests.

problems.title: The 'likely closed' flag is fed by links that aren't the shop's and by duplicates, and shoppers never see it
problems.affected_public: 45 public likely_closed. 12 of them rest on a dead platform link (7 business.site, 5 cigarplaces.com pages), and 2 are the same shop listed twice (Tin Can #29843/#29844). Sample of 3: 1 closed, 2 open. The card and profile show nothing different for these listings (closureInfo only reacts to permanently_closed or storefront='closed').
problems.how_measured: m1.js plus a host breakdown of the flagged links, 3 live checks, and a read of StoreProfile.jsx closureInfo.
examples: #27666 Torch Cigar Lounge, Montgomery AL: flagged 'no way left to contact it', but Yelp (Feb 2026), Facebook and Instagram are active and its phone (334) 300-5037 is public. Open.
#29843 Tin Can Cigar, Lynden WA: flagged, but Yelp (Nov 2025) and a WA corporate filing show it trading. Open. #29844 is the same shop.
#27021 Holy Smokes, New Smyrna Beach: flagged and truly closed (Yelp CLOSED), yet still shown like a normal listing.
#31692 Timo's Bar, Davenport IA: its 'website' is cigarplaces.com/state/florida-cigar-bars.aspx, a directory page about another state.
problems.customer_impact: About a third of flagged listings are closed, but they look identical to verified ones. Conversely, a staff member who clicks 'confirm' without checking would hide open shops such as Torch.

problems.title: Stale OSM-only pins with no phone, no website and often no address are never checked
problems.affected_public: 651 public listings have no website and no phone, and the no-contact rule never looks at them because it requires a dead website. The strongest subset is 46: OSM-only, last edited before 2020, no Overture cigar or tobacco record within 150 m, and no phone or site. 2 checked: 1 closed, 1 with no trace online.
problems.how_measured: OSM API metadata fetched for all 544 public OSM listings (4 batched requests), crossed with the Overture records in stores.json.
examples: #40248 Edward's Pipe & Tobacco Shop, Los Altos CA: OSM node version 1 from 2014, no Overture record nearby, no phone or site. Yelp says 'CLOSED - Updated November 2025'. Confirmed closed and still public.
#41658 Duke Bazzel Tobacco & Lounge, Colonie NY: OSM version 1 from 2010, no street address, and no trace anywhere online. Suspected closed.
#40592 Cigar Loft, 2448 Central Ave, St Petersburg: OSM version 1 from 2013, while #23334 'TSP Cigars formerly The Cigar Loft' is public at 1941 34th St N. Suspected old name and address.
problems.customer_impact: A pin with only a name, sometimes without even a street, sends people to a shop that closed years ago, with nothing to call first.

problems.title: Business-registry closures (BrightQuery) sometimes hide shops that still trade
problems.affected_public: 166 hidden source-closed listings would otherwise be public; 159 of them are BrightQuery records and 34 have a working website. 3 sampled: 2 truly closed, 1 open. Rough extrapolation: tens of the 166 could be open.
problems.how_measured: m3.js joined to overture_raw.json source_dataset, plus 3 live checks.
examples: #21767 Headdies Pipe Shop, Ithaca NY: hidden as 'permanently closed', but Yelp (updated July 2026) shows it trading at 110 E State St. It is mainly a pipe and vape shop.
#22235 J&M Cigars, Fairfield CT: Yelp says 'CLOSED - Updated October 2025'. Correctly hidden.
#8907 Bidwell Cigar, Chico CA: Yelp and Yellow Pages say CLOSED. Correctly hidden.
problems.customer_impact: A live shop is missing from the map, which costs it customers and costs us a shop that could claim its listing.

sweeps.name: Make closures stick (bug fix, and a prerequisite for every other sweep)
sweeps.fixes: Problem 2 (sweep closures undone on import, chain closures missing from the queue). It must ship before any new directory build, including the Overture refresh.
sweeps.method:
1) storefrontCheck skips any row whose storefront is 'closed' or 'duplicate', or whose operating_status is permanently_closed, likely_closed or closed.
2) importStores treats our own operating_status='permanently_closed' as binding for visibility, just like ruledOut. It stops writing the source's 'open' over likely_closed or permanently_closed when closed_reason is not the source default.
3) chainCheck writes operating_status='permanently_closed' instead of 'closed', so its 7 rows appear in the Closures queue.
4) Extend scratchpad test_reimport.js: seed a website-closed row, a chain-closed row and a report-closed row, run storefrontCheck then a forced import, and assert all three stay hidden.
One-off repair, from a reviewed file: set storefront='closed' again on #2585 (confirmed) and #11014. Send #8767 and #18397 to the queue for a person to decide; #8767 is probably a reopen.
sweeps.sources: Existing database and code only.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk: None for live shops, except that a wrong closure also becomes sticky. That is why #8767 Boatyard and #18397 go to a person before being made binding.
sweeps.expected_yield: Stops 4 known closures (1 confirmed) from coming back, protects 7 chain closures and every future report closure, and puts 7 rows in the review queue.
sweeps.effort: 2 to 3 hours, including the re-import test

sweeps.name: Closure reader trusts only the shop's own page
sweeps.fixes: Problem 3 (live shop hidden because of an unrelated page). Also moves 'we moved' wording to the relocation sweep instead of treating it as a closure.
sweeps.method:
In checkWebsiteForClosure, compare the registrable domain of the final URL after redirects with the listed domain. If they differ, return no opinion, unless the page names the shop (reuse the hours sweep's name-on-page check, which already rejects about 380 foreign sites).
Check the final host, not only the listed one, against NOT_THE_SHOPS_OWN_SITE, and add maps.apple.com, g.co, maps.app.goo.gl, share.google, tinyurl, bit.ly, forms.gle and parking hosts (hugedomains, expireddomains, expiredwixdomain, ww<N>. subdomains) to that list.
Send phrases like 'we've moved', 'new location' and 'visit us at our new location' to the relocation queue.
Then re-run --store on the 4 existing website closures.
sweeps.sources: Shop websites (already fetched by the sweep).
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk: A shop that points its old domain at a new domain announcing the closure would be missed. The name-on-page exception covers that case, and a missed closure only keeps a listing up, which is the safer error.
sweeps.expected_yield: Reopens 1 likely-live shop (Boatyard) after review. Stops about 360 cross-domain redirects and 20 map or shortener links from being read as the shop speaking. The same host check lets linkCheck mark the 31 lapsed or spam takeovers as dead.
sweeps.effort: 2 hours

sweeps.name: Moved-shop sweep (relocations and closed branches)
sweeps.fixes: Problem 1
sweeps.method:
Candidates come from three places:
(a) Public pairs with the same 10-digit phone and the same non-generic name words, 250 m to 40 km apart, with different street numbers (78 pairs).
(b) chainCheck 'former_branch' holdbacks where the town is still named on the chain's site (49): compare street numbers, not just the town.
(c) A hidden source-closed record at the listing's address with the same phone.
For each candidate, reuse the hours sweep's collect step: homepage plus up to 3 contact or locations pages, plus JSON-LD PostalAddress and the WP Store Locator feed. Extract street number and street name, normalized with dedupeListings.normalizeAddress, and fuzzy-match the street name (edit distance 1 or less, so 'Green' matches 'Greene').
Verdicts:
- The site names A but not B, and B shares A's phone or the site says moved: B is 'moved'. Hide B with storefront='moved' and a pointer to A, the same reversible pattern as duplicates.
- The site names a new street in B's town that no listing has (Churchill's 6030 W Behrend): propose an address change for B, geocoded from JSON-LD geo or Nominatim.
- Both addresses named: keep both.
- Neither named, or the site can't be reached: no verdict.
Write a decisions file and apply only after review, with --confirm --from like chainCheck.
sweeps.sources: Shop websites and chain locator feeds; the existing hours and chain evidence; OSM Nominatim for geocoding (free, 1 request per second).
sweeps.needs_from_mason: One decision: when the new address is not already listed, edit the old listing in place or create a new one and hide the old.
sweeps.risk: It could hide a real second branch when the site's locations page is incomplete or misread. Point Break's '403 Greene St' against the site's '403 Green St' nearly flagged a live Key West branch. Guardrails: require at least one parsed street address in the same town, require a phone match or explicit moved wording, fuzzy street matching, never act on chains with more than 10 locations without their locator feed, human review of the decisions file, and hide-with-pointer so every decision is reversible.
sweeps.expected_yield: 25 pairs are already flagged offline. 4 of the candidates I checked were real and 1 is likely. Expect roughly 20 to 40 old or closed addresses hidden or corrected.
sweeps.effort: 1 to 1.5 days to build, about 1 hour of crawling, 1 to 2 hours of review

sweeps.name: Clean up the no-contact 'likely closed' flag, extend it to stale OSM pins, and show shoppers a caveat
sweeps.fixes: Problems 5 and 6
sweeps.method:
1) Signal (c) ignores dead links on platform or directory hosts (business.site, cigarplaces.com, webs.com, godaddysites and the like) and treats them as 'no website'. That withdraws the flags that rest only on the link; 12 of the 45 today.
2) Merge duplicates before flagging (Tin Can #29843/#29844).
3) New rule for listings without a website: OSM-only, no phone, no website, no hours, last OSM edit before 2020 (batched OSM API or Overpass `out meta`, 150 ids per request), and no Overture cigar or tobacco record within 150 m. These become likely_closed (46 today). Also store OSM timestamp and version at fetch time: change `out center tags` to `out center meta`.
4) On a likely_closed listing, drop the 'Open now' badge and show 'We couldn't confirm this shop is still open. Call or check before you go.' Never auto-hide from this signal.
5) Clear the flag automatically when the listing gains a phone, a live site or hours.
sweeps.sources: The existing directory, the OSM API or Overpass (free), and linkCheck results.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: One decision: may a public caveat appear on likely_closed listings? (Recommended yes, since 1 in 3 checked was closed.)
sweeps.risk: A neutral caveat on a live shop (Torch, Tin Can) could cost it a visit. Guardrails: word it neutrally, never hide, clear it automatically on new contact data, and sort the staff queue by strength of evidence.
sweeps.expected_yield: About 12 weak flags withdrawn and about 46 stale ghost pins flagged. From the samples (1 of 3 flagged, 1 of 2 stale), maybe a third to a half of the flagged set is closed, so roughly 20 to 35 closed shops get a caveat and a staff review.
sweeps.effort: Half a day

sweeps.name: Monthly Overture refresh with change detection
sweeps.fixes: Source lag (SJ Springfield, closed by March 2025, was still 'open' in the 2026-08 release); BrightQuery closures that are wrong (Problem 7)
sweeps.method:
Each month, run the existing DuckDB extract on the newest release. Add sources[*].update_time and sources[*].dataset to the query, and diff by GERS id:
- open becomes permanently_closed: hide through the existing import path.
- The id is missing from the new release, with no same-name record within 150 m: likely_closed, and into the staff queue after two consecutive releases.
- BrightQuery-only permanently_closed where a meta, Foursquare or OSM record, or the shop's working site, says it is trading: a 'reopen review' queue. Start with the 34 hidden records that have a working website.
Use Overture's GERS changelog for removed ids where the release publishes one.
sweeps.sources: Overture S3 public bucket (free) and DuckDB.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing. The 'Make closures stick' fix must ship first.
sweeps.risk: Overture drops or replaces ids for reasons other than closure, such as merges and re-categorization. Guardrails: flag only, require two releases, check for a same-name record within 150 m, and send BrightQuery reopens to a person.
sweeps.expected_yield: Tens of new closures per month (one release marked 564 of 45,129 cigar and tobacco records closed). Of the 34 BrightQuery-closed records with a working site, perhaps 5 to 15 are live and could come back (from a sample of 1 in 3).
sweeps.effort: Half a day to build, then about 30 minutes a month

sweeps.name: Paid business-status lookup for the pool no free source can settle
sweeps.fixes: Problems 4, 5 and 6: the residual closed shops among the 1,278 dead-website listings with a phone and the 696 no-contact listings
sweeps.method: Look up Google Places business_status, either when a listing is viewed or once in a batch for the riskiest roughly 2,000 listings (dead site, no contact, stale OSM, BrightQuery). Accept a match only when the name is similar and the place is within 100 m. Cache only the place_id and the status, per Google's terms. CLOSED_PERMANENTLY goes into a reviewed hide file; CLOSED_TEMPORARILY gets the caveat. The same call can fill missing phones (Torch's is public). Yelp's is_closed field would also work, but the Fusion API is paid and scraping Yelp is against its terms.
sweeps.sources: Google Places API (paid)
sweeps.needs_from_mason: An API key with billing, a budget, and acceptance of the storage terms. Google replaced the $200 monthly credit with per-SKU free caps in 2025, so check current pricing before relying on the worklog's estimate.
sweeps.risk: Google may match a different business at the same address. The name-and-distance guardrail and review before hiding cover that.
sweeps.expected_yield: The samples suggest well under a quarter of the dead-site pool is closed, so perhaps 50 to 150 closures across roughly 2,000 lookups. That is an extrapolation with wide error.
sweeps.effort: 1 day to build, plus Google charges

audits.already_covered:
- Overture operating_status is read and applied on import. 560 records are marked permanently_closed, and the 162 that were public were hidden. BrightQuery is behind most of these; my sample of 3 found 2 truly closed and 1 still trading, so it is mostly right.
- The website closure reader has sensible guards: day and holiday words, 'temporarily' and 'reopens', negation, third-party widgets, a list of platform hosts, and ticket or registration sentences. It found Redland (confirmed closed on its own site). Its only failure I found comes from following a redirect to another domain.
- The no-contact rule only produces likely_closed and never hides. That is the right call: 2 of the 3 flagged listings I checked are open.
- Visitor reports need 2 independent votes, all anonymous reports together count as one, and claimed or staff-edited listings are protected. No closure report exists yet (the only report is a smoke test).
- chainCheck hid 7 closed branches with corroboration, and correctly held back most doubtful cases. One holdback, Churchill's Glendale, turns out to be a move within the same town.
- linkCheck treats 403/429 as blocked rather than dead and hides dead links on listings. It re-checks up to 500 sites every 12 hours.
- In the admin queue, confirm and reopen both set staff_edited, so staff decisions survive sweeps and imports.
- Claimed listings are never touched by any closure code (0 public listings are claimed).
- Not done yet, and not to be redone as written: the worklog's 'dead website plus no phone' idea and the '$200 free credit' Google plan. My sample shows a dead site alone is not evidence of a closure. The 'two consecutive Overture releases' idea from the worklog is still open and appears here as the Overture refresh sweep.
audits.open_questions:
- Moved shops: when the new address is not listed yet (Churchill's Glendale), should the old listing's address and pin be edited in place, or should a new listing be created and the old one hidden with a pointer?
- Should likely_closed listings show shoppers a 'couldn't confirm it's still open, call first' caveat and lose the 'Open now' badge?
- Is a Google Places key with billing acceptable? The dead-website pool can't be settled for free: 11 of 11 sampled were open, so the closed ones in it are a small share that only a status lookup will find.
- BrightQuery-closed records: accept them as they are, or run a reopen review on the 34 that have working websites?
- Is a pipe and vape head shop like Headdies in scope for the map at all? That decides whether reopening it matters.
- Visitor reports: one signed-in account plus any anonymous report hides an unclaimed listing. Should a competitor-resistant rule, such as two signed-in reporters or a corroborating machine signal, be required before hiding?
- I did not execute the import to demonstrate the regression (read-only). It is shown from code and row state, so the re-import test in the first sweep should confirm it before and after the fix.

audits.current_state:
HOW VISIBILITY IS DECIDED. buildDirectory.normalizeOverture maps each Overture primary category to OSM-style tags (tobacco_shop to shop=tobacco, cigar_bar to amenity=bar plus club=cigar, lounge to amenity=lounge, e_cigarette_store to shop=e-cigarette, and so on). It also copies club=cigar and any non-convenience `shop` value from the alternate categories, so an alternate `e_cigarette_store` becomes shop=e-cigarette. importStores then re-runs osm.classify(name, ctags, website) on every row and sets visible = confidence >= 0.5. Rows closed at source, rows with storefront in (not_retail, online_only, closed, duplicate), and staff-edited rows are the exceptions. The importer drops the -0.15 nudge that buildDirectory applies for low Overture existence confidence. storefrontCheck then overrides with a category allow-list plus name rules, and its not_retail verdict is binding on re-import.

The classify() score is a name-regex model:
- Base: 0.8 for shop=cigar or club=cigar, 0.45 for shop=tobacco, 0.2 for any amenity, 0.1 otherwise.
- +0.45 for a cigar or brand word; +0.1 for tobacco, pipe or snuff.
- +0.25 if the website domain matches /cigar|humidor|tobacconist|stogie|habano|lounge/.
- -0.15 for a "smoke" word; -0.2 for a mild word (discount, outlet, superstore, mart, market, express, stop, land, city, world, zone, plus, dollar, beer, wine); -0.45 for a strong word (vape, hookah, cbd, glass, cigarettes, liquor, gas...).
- -0.6 for shop=e-cigarette, cannabis or convenience.

Overture's tobacco_shop category sits at 0.45, so the 0.5 line reduces to a name test. A name containing "Tobacco" or "Pipe" scores 0.55 and is public. A neutral name scores 0.45 and is hidden. A "Smoke" name scores 0.30 and is hidden.

MEASURED (node scripts over stores.json joined to store_directory.json.gz by source:source_id, 0 unmatched; scripts in C:/Users/mason/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Users-mason-OneDrive-Desktop-cigarApp/a956c8ab-bec6-4085-b83b-7fcd97853bc4/scratchpad/audit/work/relcov/):
- Public: 7,431. 5,050 (68%) have Overture category tobacco_shop. 3,083 sit at exactly 0.55.
- Hidden with storefront='yes': 22,133. 21,642 of them are not closed at source, and 18,733 of those have category tobacco_shop.
- Of those 21,642, only 2 have a checked website_status, although 10,285 have a website. The link, closure and hours sweeps only ever ran on public rows.

Public listings by evidence band:
- A, cigar word in the name and no vape/hookah word: 4,008.
- D, only "Tobacco" or "Pipe" in the name: 3,001.
- B, cigar word plus a vape, hookah or cigarette word: 118.
- C, Overture cigar_bar category with no cigar word: 122.
- E, public only through the website bonus: 153.
- F, bar or lounge category with no cigar word: 29.

Desk review of random samples (fixed seed):
- Band A, 40 listings: 38 read as real cigar shops or lounges. 8 of the 40 have dead domains (dns_fail or parked).
- Band D, 60 listings: 5 cigar-focused, 12 in chains confirmed to sell cigars, about 34 general tobacco shops, and 9 that are not places to buy cigars (15%; 95% CI about 8-26%).
- Hidden neutral-named listings in 22 metros, 70 listings: almost all head, vape or cannabis-accessory shops or unrelated businesses.
- Hidden listings with their own websites, 16: none cigar-focused.

About 27 live lookups in total, detailed per problem below.

sweeps.name: Classifier fix and diff-reviewed re-score
sweeps.fixes: Problems 1, 3 and 4, and the classifier half of 6
sweeps.method:
Change osm.classify and buildDirectory:
(a) The domain bonus uses /cigar(?!et)|humidor|tobacconist|stogie|habano/, and 'lounge' counts only alongside a cigar word.
(b) An alternate e_cigarette_store no longer sets shop=e-cigarette. A primary e_cigarette_store penalty is capped at -0.15 when the name has cigar vocabulary.
(c) Add havana|habana|maduro|robusto|vitola|churchill|tabac(o|aria|alera|queria)?|cigar[a-z]+ (excluding cigaret*) to the cigar vocabulary, and 'tabacco' to TOBACCO_RE.
(d) Skip NEG_MILD when the name has cigar vocabulary.
(e) Add vapes|vapez|kava|710|dabs?|bongs?|hydro|headshop|peace pipe|pipe dreamz?|ecig to NEG_STRONG.
(f) Type cigar_lounge (and the Lounge tag) only with cigar vocabulary in the name or domain, never from Overture cigar_bar alone when the name says smoke, vape, mart or deli.
(g) Carry Overture's existence confidence into the importer's re-score.
Run a dry run that writes a diff file: rows that would flip public to hidden and hidden to public, with the triggering rule. Flips to public do NOT go live in this sweep; they feed the rescue sweep. Flips to hidden are applied only after review, as storefront='not_retail' with a reason so the importer honours them.
sweeps.sources: store_directory.json.gz (ctags, raw categories), the stores table
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing (approve the diff)
sweeps.risk: A regex change can flip hundreds of rows at once. Adding 'dab' or 'hydro' could hit a real shop. Guardrails: apply only from a reviewed diff; never hide a row with a cigar or brand word; never touch claimed or staff_edited rows; add self-tests for the named examples (#5413, #22109, #12898 must pass; #4581, #6466, #10186 must fail).
sweeps.expected_yield: About 60-100 public rows to review for hiding: the cigarette and lounge domain cases, pipe-named head shops, and vape-named rows. The 69 e-cigarette-tag victims plus about 150 vocabulary misses go to the rescue sweep.
sweeps.effort: Half a day of code and tests, a 10-minute dry run, 1-2 hours of review

sweeps.name: Cigar-vocabulary rescue with live verification
sweeps.fixes: Problems 1, 2 and 8
sweeps.method:
Candidates are the 549 rows in rc_hidden_cigar_candidates.json plus rc_notretail_cigar_candidates.json. Run the existing linkCheck, closureCheck and hoursSweep collect over them; these rows have never been checked.
Accept a row when:
- the website works, the page names the shop, and the page shows cigar evidence (humidor, a premium brand list, 'cigar lounge'); or
- it has no working site, but has a phone, Overture existence confidence >= 0.9, the meta or Foursquare dataset, and no public listing within 150 m with a matching name (namesMatch).
Reject a row for closure text, a dead domain with no phone, a site that is a factory or brand page with no street address (like #16977), or an Overture permanently_closed flag.
Write storefront='yes', a new storefront_reason of 'rescued: <evidence>', and visible=1. Because the importer recomputes visible from classify, either land the classifier fix first or add 'rescued' to the verdicts the importer honours. Use the hours and web_image evidence from the same pass.
sweeps.sources: Shop websites (existing collect code), Overture ov_confidence and dataset, the stores table
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing. Optional: a Google Places key to confirm business_status on rescued rows that have no website.
sweeps.risk: Publishing a closed or moved shop (Annapolis Cigar Co, Capital Cigar's stale address) or a factory brand. Guardrails: require live corroboration; update the address from the site's structured data when it disagrees, or leave the row for review; human review of every rescued row with no website.
sweeps.expected_yield: About 250-350 real, open cigar shops and lounges added, roughly 100-130 of them in the 22 largest metros
sweeps.effort: 1 day to wire up by reusing hoursSweep and closureCheck, about 1 hour to run, 2-3 hours of review

sweeps.name: Precision sweep of weak public bands
sweeps.fixes: Problems 3, 4, 5 and 6
sweeps.method:
Auto-mark not_retail (with a reason) only the unambiguous cases:
- the 56 manufacturer, B2B and landmark rows, after a quick review list (keep the J.C. Newman factory store and La Casa del Habano);
- non-shop place names: trail, RV resort, marina, engine club, 'No Public Sales', an association office.
For the rest of bands D, E, F and C (3,305 rows; 1,098 of band D have a working site), collect full homepage and navigation text, not only the lines near the hours as the hours sweep kept. Score cigar evidence (humidor, cigar brand names, 'premium cigars') against other-trade evidence (bong, dab, rig, glass, kratom, delta-8, THC, CBD, e-juice, plumbing).
Send a row to the admin queue with that evidence when it has no cigar evidence and has strong other-trade evidence. Hide it only after human review.
For the 1,451 band-D rows without a website, use only name rules and Overture alternate categories (e_cigarette_store, cannabis_clinic, glass). They go to the queue, never to auto-hide.
Fix the Lounge badge on cigar_bar-category smoke shops unless the site shows a lounge.
sweeps.sources: Shop websites, Overture alternate categories, existing hours_evidence and chain_evidence files
sweeps.needs_from_mason: A decision on members-only lounges (23 named 'private' or 'members'): a badge rather than hiding is recommended.
sweeps.risk: Hiding a general tobacco shop that does keep a humidor but has a vape-heavy homepage. Guardrails: never auto-hide with any cigar evidence; queue rather than hide; claimed and staff_edited rows untouched; storefront='not_retail' so re-import honours it.
sweeps.expected_yield: About 40 auto-hidden non-shops, about 300-600 queued for review (about 150-450 hidden after review), and about 45 false Lounge badges removed
sweeps.effort: 1.5 days, about 1-2 hours of collection (plus the browser pass for JavaScript sites), 3-4 hours of review

sweeps.name: Scope decision and consistent chain-level cigar-focus flag
sweeps.fixes: Problem 7
sweeps.method: Mason decides whether general tobacco shops that carry cigars belong in the directory. Wild Bill's, Smoker Friendly and Tobacco Superstore are the test cases: Wild Bill's is shown today, the other two are mostly hidden. Then apply one verdict per chain domain: the 147 split domains and 693 hidden branches get the verdict of their public siblings, or the siblings follow them. Add a cigar_focus field ('premium' when website or chain evidence shows a humidor or premium brands, 'general', or 'unknown'). Rank premium first and offer a 'Walk-in humidor' filter, so that including general shops does not bury cigar-focused ones.
sweeps.sources: The chain evidence already collected, chain websites, the stores table
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Product decision: cigar-focused only, or every shop that sells cigars
sweeps.risk: Including general shops adds about 700 or more pins with limited selection; excluding them removes about 2,000 current public rows. Guardrails: decide by chain with evidence, and review a sample per chain.
sweeps.expected_yield: A consistent, explainable rule in place of the name-based 0.5 cut. Either about 700 chain branches added, or about 1,500-2,000 general shops demoted or hidden.
sweeps.effort: A decision plus half a day of work and 1-2 hours of review

sweeps.name: Extract-coverage top-up for lounges without 'cigar' in the name
sweeps.fixes: Problem 9
sweeps.method: Extend the DuckDB Overture query (bottom of buildDirectory.js) to bars, lounges, cocktail bars, whisky bars and speakeasies whose name or website contains cigar vocabulary or brand names (macanudo, montecristo, davidoff, padron, fuente, rocky patel). Add OSM bars with club=cigar or smoking=yes plus a cigar word. Rebuild the directory and run the new rows through the rescue sweep's verification.
sweeps.sources: Overture places (S3 parquet, free), OSM Overpass
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk: Pulls in bars that only mention cigars on a menu. Guardrail: require the rescue sweep's cigar evidence on the website.
sweeps.expected_yield: Tens of listings, but high-value ones in major cities (e.g. Club Macanudo, if still open)
sweeps.effort: Half a day, plus a rebuild and a review pass

audits.already_covered: storefrontCheck works well for its purpose. It removed 537 wrong-category non-shops (the Cigar City brewery, barbershop and title company), wholesalers, online stores and Bitcoin ATMs. Its category allow-list does cut the long tail, and the importer honours its verdicts. Overture's permanently_closed flag and closureCheck already hide source-confirmed and website-announced closures. dedupeListings and chainCheck handle duplicates and closed branches. linkCheck already hides dead links on public rows. A probe of 44 well-known shops found nearly all of them present and public: Davidoff, Smoke Inn, Two Guys, Iwan Ries, Up Down Cigar, JR Cigar, Cigars International, Tinder Box, Corona Cigar. So the cigar-named core, band A (4,008 rows, about 95% genuine in a 40-row sample), is in good shape apart from dead domains, which belong to the closure work. What nobody has done: any precision or recall sweep on classifier scores, any check of the 21,642 hidden storefront='yes' rows (no link, closure or hours data), or a reversal path for storefrontCheck's category rejections of cigar-named shops. The worklog's 'spot-check the launch metro in the admin queue' is the only related to-do.
audits.open_questions:
1. Scope: is CigarBuddy for cigar-focused shops (humidor, premium brands) or any shop that sells cigars? This decides whether about 700 hidden chain branches such as Smoker Friendly and Tobacco Superstore come in, or about 1,500-2,000 public general tobacco shops go out.
2. Members-only lounges (23 public named 'private' or 'members'): hide them, or show a 'Members only' badge?
3. Where a hidden shop's own site gives a different address (Capital Cigar #12831), should the rescue update the address automatically or queue it?
4. The precision estimate for the 3,001 'Tobacco'/'Pipe'-named rows rests on a 60-row desk sample plus chain evidence. A larger website-evidence pass would narrow the 8-26% interval.
5. The 289 not_retail cigar-named candidates have only 2 live checks, both inconclusive, so their real-shop share (guessed at 40-60%) is unmeasured.
6. Are Club Macanudo, Shelly's Back Room and Burn Naples still open? Not verified.
7. tobaccosuper.com now serves an unrelated Japanese site while 4 public rows show website_status 'ok', so linkCheck may need a content check. That belongs to the website auditor.

Raw signals among public listings (addresses normalised by house number + street words, with suites removed, spelled numerals turned into digits and FL-44/SR 44/US-60/Route forms unified):
- Same street address in the same ZIP or city: 278 pairs, 520 listings. 143 pairs look like one business; 135 are different businesses in one building.
- Same phone: 343 pairs, 479 listings on 223 numbers. 186 are duplicate candidates. 157 are chains with one central number (Tobacco Hut: 11 listings on (540) 538-5920) or twins in other towns.
- Same website + same city: 243 pairs, 394 listings. 144 pairs (93 groups, 212 listings) are chain branches with different phones; 99 are duplicate candidates.
- Similar name within 150 m: 48 pairs, 96 listings. 47 are duplicates.

Tiers (union-find over pairs):
- T1, same door + same name, confirmed by the same phone or website, or one twin is a bare map record: 73 clusters, 148 listings, 75 extra rows.
- T1b, same door + same phone and same website, different names: 18 extra rows.

- Union of all tiers: 232 clusters, 474 public listings (6.4%), 242 extra rows. From the hand-review and web checks I estimate about 180–210 of those are true duplicates, 2.5–2.8% of the map.

Kept as real (not duplicates): 93 same-town chain groups, and 212 clusters (451 listings) of different businesses sharing a building. Holt's #20611 with Ashton Cigar Bar #20612 upstairs is one example.

The twins disagree with each other. Across 249 twin pairs:

- the Lounge badge differs in 67;

problems.title: Why they survived: the dedupe job and the build's name matcher are too narrow, and the importer never retires a folded row
problems.affected_public: All of the above. Specifically, 41 public OSM rows are same-door, same-name twins of an Overture row.
problems.how_measured: Ran dedupeListings on today's snapshot: 0 merges. Of 83 same-door same-name pairs, 65 fail its exact-name grouping. 14 are more than 200 m apart with differently spelled addresses ('Twelve Mile'/'12 Mile', 'State Rd 200'/'SW Highway 200'). 4 have different city labels ('Berlin Twp'/'Ionia', 'Marshall Twp'/'Wexford', 'Carmel Hamlet'/'Carmel', 'Round Rock'/'Georgetown'). For the 45 OSM+Overture pairs, 41 were already within 150 m and failed only osm.js namesMatch. Read importStores.js: it only updates rows present in the new file.
examples: nameKey output: "cole s tobacco" vs "coles tobacco"; "j and j tobacco" vs "jandj tobacco"; "stogies" vs "stogie s"; "smoke stack cigar" vs "smokestack cigar"; "d l tobacco" vs "dl tobacco"; "jr cigars clayton" vs "jr cigars" (2-letter words ignored); "tobacconist greenwich" vs "tobacconist" (the town word blocks the match). All return false (verified by running osm.js).
The reverse error: namesMatch treats a town name as distinctive, so Bellevue Cigar matches 'Tobacco Bellevue', a different business.
buildDirectory lets an Overture record absorb only one OSM twin (the `!t.osm_id` guard).
importStores never touches rows missing from a rebuilt directory, so fixing the matcher alone would fold the twins in the file but leave the 41 OSM rows public forever.
problems.customer_impact: Existing duplicates stay public, and every rebuild re-creates the same kind of twin.

sweeps.name: Same-door merge v2 (extend dedupeListings.js)
sweeps.fixes: Problem 1, and the existing rows behind problem 5
sweeps.method:
Candidates: visible=1, claimed=0, staff_edited=0.

Same door: same house number (first numeric token, any length) and at least 50% of street words shared after normalising (suite/unit/#/floor removed; Twelve→12, First→1st; FL-44/SR 44/State Rd 44/Route 10/US-60/NJ-10 → 'hwy N'; directions and street types dropped), with the same ZIP or city. Or pins within 60 m.

Same shop: names equal after lowercasing and removing apostrophes, '&', spaces and plural s. Or the distinctive words, with trade words AND the listing's town name removed, squash-equal, one containing the other (6+ characters and not only common words like Havana/Casa/Royal), or at least 50% overlap allowing an edit distance of 1 on words of 5+ letters.

AUTO tier: same door + same shop + (same phone, or same website host, or one twin has no phone and no website AND the same house number or no street address). Measured: 73 pairs.

REVIEW tier: same name but different house numbers (4 pairs), conflicting phones and sites (6), clusters of 3+, and pins more than 1 km apart, which go through the pin check first.

Survivor order: the row holding inventory, followers or reviews; then the pin agreeing with a geocode of its address (or OSM-corroborated); then a working website that names the shop; then hours_source='website'; then the existing richness() score. Fill the survivor's empty fields from the twin (phone, website, hours plus hours_source, has_lounge, web_image_url) without overwriting anything. Hide the rest with visible=0, storefront='duplicate', storefront_reason='Same shop as listing #N' (importStores already honours 'duplicate'). Re-point child rows to the survivor.

Write a dry-run CSV, review it, and apply only the reviewed file. Afterwards, run the auto tier at the end of every import.
sweeps.sources: stores table only, plus geocodes from the pin-check sweep
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk: It could merge two different shops in one strip mall or at neighbouring doors: Bellevue Cigar (565 Lincoln Ave) and a separate tobacco dealer at 553 would have been merged on the town name alone. Guardrails: the town name never counts toward a name match; different house numbers or conflicting phones and sites go to review; never touch claimed or staff_edited rows; hide, never delete, with the pointer reason so every decision can be reversed; review the whole dry run (about 80 rows).
sweeps.expected_yield: About 70 extra listings hidden automatically and about 5–10 more after review, of 75 measured
sweeps.effort: Build 3–4 h (normaliser, name folding, tiers, self-tests from the pairs above); run under 1 min; review 1 h

sweeps.name: One door, several names: stale-name resolver
sweeps.fixes: Problem 2
sweeps.sources: stores table; cached website and chain evidence in the scratchpad; live re-fetch of about 100 shop sites (hoursRender for JS sites)
sweeps.needs_from_mason: A decision: should a shop and its in-house lounge that share one phone and address (JR Cigar + Casa de Montecristo ×3, House of Cigar + HOC D.Ellan Lounge ×2, Wild Bill's + WB Madison Cigar Lounge, Big Daddy's + Fat Stogies) be one listing or two?
sweeps.risk: It could hide a live second venue, or keep the stale name as the survivor. Guardrails: positive evidence for the survivor is required; different phones plus different working sites means keep both (Holt's + Ashton); every decision is reviewed; hide, never delete.
sweeps.expected_yield: About 55–75 stale-name listings hidden (all 6 checked clusters were stale)
sweeps.effort: Build 3 h; fetch 15 min; review 2 h (or reviewer agents)

sweeps.name: Moved-shop check (extend chainCheck.js to phone+name groups)
sweeps.fixes: Problem 3
sweeps.method:
Candidates: same name + same phone, same ZIP or city, different street (65 clusters, 68 extra rows).

chainCheck only groups listings that share a website; group these by phone + name instead, so a listing without a site (#23521) is judged from its sibling's site. Fetch the homepage and /contact, /locations, /about (rendered for JS sites), plus the cached chain feeds.

Decision:
- If the site says 'new location', 'moved' or 'relocated' and names one street, hide the other listing.
- Otherwise hide a listing only if all four hold: (i) the site works and names the business; (ii) it publishes at least one full street address; (iii) the listing's house number appears nowhere on the site (match the number first, then a fuzzy street name, so 'Greene' vs 'Green' cannot fail); (iv) the site publishes at least as many addresses as the listings we keep.
- Unreachable site or no site: no action.

Write a reviewed decisions file and apply it with --from, as chainCheck already does.
sweeps.sources: shop websites (live and cached), chain store-locator feeds, OSM for tie-breaks
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk: It could hide a real branch that shares one phone: Point Break Cigars has 5 Key West stores on one number, and its site spells '403 Green St.' where our listing has 'Greene'. Guardrails: house-number matching, the address-coverage rule, no action without a readable site, a reviewed file, hide never delete.
sweeps.expected_yield: About 45–55 stale addresses hidden (6 of 7 checked clusters had one)
sweeps.effort: Build 3–4 h reusing chainCheck extraction; crawl 20–40 min; review 1.5 h

sweeps.name: Twin pin check with the US Census geocoder
sweeps.fixes: Problem 4, and correct survivor choice in the first three sweeps
sweeps.method:
For every twin pair with pins more than 300 m apart (35 T1/T1b pairs), and for cross-town twins found by same name + same phone + same house number or no address (#39731, #10839), geocode each street address with the US Census Bureau geocoder. Its batch CSV takes up to 10,000 rows, is free and needs no key; Nominatim at 1 request/s is the fallback and importStores already uses it.

Keep the pin within 250 m of an exact-match geocode, and copy it to the survivor if the survivor's pin is the wrong one. Flag any row whose own pin is more than 1 km from its geocode, and recompute its timezone (Sam Hills in Prescott currently runs on America/Denver). Leave rows whose address doesn't geocode untouched.
sweeps.sources: US Census geocoder, Nominatim, osm_id already on rows
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk: Geocoders mis-place rural and highway addresses (M-66, US-131 BUS). Act only on exact-match results, and only when the other twin's pin agrees within 250 m; send everything else to review.
sweeps.expected_yield: 35+ pairs settled; about 26 wrong pins corrected (the pairs more than 1 km apart) plus 2 wrong-state twins
sweeps.effort: Build 2 h; geocoding takes minutes; review 30 min

sweeps.name: Stop re-creating duplicates: build matcher + importer absorption
sweeps.fixes: Problem 5 (root cause); keeps the other sweeps from having to repeat
sweeps.method:
(1) osm.js nameKey/namesMatch: remove apostrophes before splitting (Cole's → coles), drop '&' and join single-letter initials (J & J = J&J), compare space-squashed keys (Smoke Stack = Smokestack), fold plural s, keep 2-letter initials (JR, DL, EZ, 3D), and drop the record's town name from both names. Add self-tests for the 13 misses listed above, plus negatives: Tobacco Town/Tobacco Row, Taylor Tobacco/River Tobacco, Bellevue Cigar/Tobacco Bellevue, Holt's/Ashton.
(2) buildDirectory: let one Overture record absorb every OSM record of the same shop, instead of stopping at one (the `!t.osm_id` guard), or emit an also_osm_ids list.
(3) importStores: when a directory record's osm_id or also_osm_ids names an existing OSM row with a different DB id, hide that row with storefront='duplicate' pointing at the record's row (unless claimed or staff_edited). Log rows absent from the new file for review instead of silently leaving them public.
(4) Run the same-door merge's auto tier after each import.
sweeps.sources: code; server/src/data/store_directory.json.gz
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk: A looser matcher could fold two real neighbouring shops in the build, and the importer would then hide the second. Guardrails: keep the 150 m cap; diff the fold list before and after (expect about 41 new folds, listed for review); prove it with scratchpad/test_reimport.js against a scratch database.
sweeps.expected_yield: Retires the ~41 public OSM twins at the next import and stops new ones from appearing
sweeps.effort: Code + tests 3 h; review the fold diff 1 h

Scripts and outputs are in C:/Users/mason/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Users-mason-OneDrive-Desktop-cigarApp/a956c8ab-bec6-4085-b83b-7fcd97853bc4/scratchpad/audit/work/location/. The per-listing flag list is location_flags.json (247 flags).

- 266 (3.6%) have no ZIP. 3 ZIPs are malformed: "Missiouri", "5645", and "N9A" (a Canadian postcode).

Pin accuracy (main measurement):
- Method: I geocoded all 7,120 street addresses with the free Census batch geocoder (3 requests, Public_AR_Current). Results: 5,472 Exact, 1,084 Non_Exact, 40 Tie, 524 No_Match.
- Distance from the pin to the listing's own address, over the 6,556 matches: median 56 m, p90 220 m, p95 392 m, p99 3.7 km.
- Pins more than 0.5 km off: 253. More than 1 km: 153 (76 of them Exact matches, 55 of those on ordinary non-highway streets). More than 5 km: 47. More than 10 km: 22. More than 50 km: 4.

Calibration against the chain's own coordinates (Wild Bill's store-locator feed, 2 requests, 78 listings matched):
- Our pins: median error 30 m; 6 are more than 1 km off. 2 of those are confirmed pin errors: Paw Paw (1.6 km) and Sault Ste. Marie (2.5 km).
- The Census geocoder was the one that was wrong on 5 highway-style addresses ("400 US-41": 8.9 km). A disagreement on a highway address therefore needs a third source.
- On ordinary street addresses, 11 of 11 sampled disagreements of 5 km or more had the pin wrong (3 by web search, 8 by a Nominatim third geocode that agreed with Census).

Other checks:
- **ZIP prefix vs listed state:** 13 public mismatches (37 across all 42,923 rows).
- **Pin vs ZIP centroid (Census ZCTA gazetteer):** median 2.6 km; 38 flagged above max(10 km, 3x the ZIP's radius). Most real errors overlap the geocode set; Key West is a ZCTA artifact.
- **The simplified state outlines in geo.js** put 44 pins in a neighbouring state and 105 outside every state. Almost all are border or island artifacts (Iron Mountain, Jeffersonville, Key West, Staten Island), and Windsor, Ontario falls inside Michigan. The file is too coarse to use as a check on its own.
- **Time zones:** I compared the stored zone with the tz-lookup library at the pin, by UTC offset in summer and winter. 29 differ; add 2 wrong-state records whose pins are also wrong, for 31 real errors. 11 of those listings have hours, so their open/closed badge is an hour off.
- **City names vs Census places, county subdivisions and GeoNames postal cities:** 165 not recognized. That breaks down as 2 USPS abbreviations, 35 county names, 122 township/"Town of" names, and a handful of wrong-state cities. Separately, 66 cities have damaged capitals (Mcallen, Winston-salem), and 22 cities are spelled two or more ways within one state (37 rows on the minority spelling).
- **City-centroid pins are not a pattern.** Only 2 of the 153 misplaced pins sit within 0.5 km of a Census place centre, against a 6.4% baseline. The 59 pins within 150 m of a centre are real downtown shops whose addresses geocode within about 150 m. The city-cluster outlier test (pin more than 25 km from the median of its city's listings) found 6, 3 of them already in the geocode set.
- **Foreign places:** a tz-lookup scan of all 42,923 rows plus phone and postcode patterns found 2 public (Windsor, Ontario; a Lebanese "Tobacco Bar" in Lebanon CT). There are no Cuba, Bahamas or Mexico leaks.
- **Addresses vs the shop's own site:** 282 single-location sites publish a schema.org street address I could compare. 234 give the same house number. 48 differ, of which about 9 look like relocations after removing wrong-website cases and neighbouring numbers.
- **Address text:** 76 addresses have no house number (about 30 of them unusable), 207 contain double spaces, 6 have stray whitespace, 1 is a PO Box.

External lookups used: 26 (7 page fetches, 9 web searches, 8 Nominatim, 2 chain-feed calls), plus the Census, GeoNames and tz-lookup reference downloads.

importStores.js:227: fillTimezones only fills rows where timezone IS NULL, so fixing a state or pin leaves the old zone in place.

buildDirectory.js:74 trusts Overture's region without checking it against the pin or ZIP. fetchOsmStores.js:74 forces the simplified-outline state over the OSM addr:state tag, which is how Claymont DE became PA and Plaistow NH became MA.
routes/stores.js:423: when an owner edits the address, the pin is not re-geocoded and the zone is not recomputed.
problems.customer_impact: A fix would silently come undone after a deploy, and wrong states would keep arriving from the source.

sweeps.name: 0. Make location fixes stick (prerequisite)
sweeps.fixes: The code-level problem; required before sweeps 1-5
sweeps.method: Add columns location_source ('directory'|'geocode'|'site'|'chain'|'staff'|'owner'), location_checked_at, prev_lat, prev_lng and prev_address. In importStores.js, keep address, city, state, zip, lat and lng whenever location_source is not 'directory' (or when staff_edited is set). Any write that changes state, lat or lng also recomputes timezone. The owner PUT route re-geocodes and recomputes the zone when the address changes. Prove it with a forced re-import against a scratch database, as scratchpad/test_reimport.js did for the storefront sweep.
sweeps.sources: Code only
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk: None to shops. Without it, every sweep below is reverted at the next directory build.
sweeps.expected_yield: Keeps the roughly 350 corrections below in place
sweeps.effort: 2-3 h including the re-import test

sweeps.name: 1. Time zone from the pin, not from longitude lines
sweeps.fixes: Wrong time zone (31 public, 11 badges)
sweeps.method: Replace the longitude rules in storeHours.splitState with a boundary lookup. Either vendor tz-lookup (73 KB; built from the timezone-boundary-builder / OSM boundaries) behind a whitelist of US zones, or build a county-to-zone table from the Census county gazetteer plus about 15 split-county overrides. Add a manual override for Phenix City / Russell County AL (keeps Eastern). If the lookup returns a non-US zone for a US-state listing, fall back to the state rule: the lookup is coarse near the Canadian border and called Houlton ME and Sault Ste. Marie MI Canadian. Recompute every row (not only NULLs), print the diff, review it (about 31 public rows plus hidden ones), then apply. Add self-tests for Chattanooga, East Ridge, Houghton, Negaunee, Glasgow KY, La Porte, Michigan City, Mandan, Crossville and Phenix City.
sweeps.sources: tz-lookup (CDN copy) or the Census county gazetteer; coordinates already stored
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk: A wrong zone flips a badge for a whole town. Guardrails: only change rows whose UTC offsets actually differ, keep the US-zone whitelist and state fallback, and review the full diff (small).
sweeps.expected_yield: 31 public listings corrected, 11 open/closed badges fixed; covers future imports in split states
sweeps.effort: 2 h build + 30 min review

sweeps.name: 2. Pin-vs-address geocode check
sweeps.fixes: Map pins far from the shop
sweeps.method: Collect: run the Census batch geocoder (free, no key, up to 10k per request) on every public address. For every disagreement over 1 km, get a second opinion from Nominatim (structured search, 1 request/second, about 150-300 calls). Where a chain store locator exists, use its coordinates: hoursSweep already downloads the WP Store Locator JSON but throws the lat/lng away, so keep it. Decide: auto-move a pin only when all of these hold: (a) an ordinary street address, not a highway-style one (US-41, SR-, FM, Hwy, Route, Business Spur, frontage roads); (b) Census gives an Exact match and Nominatim a house-level match within 250 m of each other; (c) both are more than 1 km from the pin; (d) the move is at most 50 km; (e) the address is backed by the shop's own site or chain feed (same house number) or by the geocoder returning the listing's ZIP. Everything else goes to a review file: highway addresses, disagreements between the geocoders, and moves over 50 km (which are usually whole-record garbage). The shop's schema.org geo counts only as a tiebreaker when its address matches ours; measured, it is often a rounded town point. Apply: write lat/lng with location_source='geocode' and keep the previous coordinates. Never touch claimed, owner-set or staff-set rows. Hide nothing.
sweeps.sources: Census Geocoder batch API; Nominatim; chain locator feeds; hours-sweep evidence
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing (the owner may approve the review file)
sweeps.risk: If the shop has moved and our address is stale, the pin gets moved to the old address. Highway geocodes are unreliable: the Census was wrong by 2-9 km on 5 Wild Bill's stores whose pins were right. Guardrails: the highway exclusion, two agreeing geocoders, the address-corroboration rule, running sweep 4 first (a site address that differs goes to review), and reviewing 30 decisions by hand before apply.
sweeps.expected_yield: 153 flagged today. About 50 auto-moves (the 55 ordinary-street cases, 11 of 11 sampled confirmed wrong) and about 100 for review, of which roughly half are real. About 100-130 pins fixed.
sweeps.effort: 1 day build, 1 h run, 2-3 h review

sweeps.name: 3. State, town and country consistency
sweeps.fixes: Wrong state, town or country; stops recurrence at build time
sweeps.method: Signals per row: a static ZIP-prefix-to-state table; a phone area-code-to-state table (NANPA); whether GeoNames lists the city in that state; the pin's state from a detailed boundary file (Census cartographic 1:500k, not the 89 KB simplified outlines, which misfile 44 border pins and put Windsor, Ontario inside Michigan); a Canadian postcode pattern; a phone country code other than +1. Rules: change the state only when the ZIP prefix and at least one of (pin state, area code, city-in-state) agree on the same other state. If the pin also sits in the wrong town, re-geocode from the backed-up address (sweep 2 rules). Foreign places are marked storefront='foreign' and hidden, which the importer must honour, after review. Records with three or more contradictions (Cigar Crafted, Cigar Vibes, Mort's, Vip smoke, 'Cigars' with ZIP 99931) are hidden pending review. Build-time: in buildDirectory.normalizeOverture, check Overture's region against the ZIP prefix and the pin; in fetchOsmStores, keep addr:state and addr:postcode and prefer them when they agree.
sweeps.sources: Static ZIP and area-code tables, GeoNames US postal file (CC-BY), Census state boundaries, existing phone/ZIP fields
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Decision: hide foreign and self-contradicting records, or attempt to repair them
sweeps.risk: A foreign phone alone is not proof: Puro Estilo Cigars (+972 phone) is a genuine Bethlehem PA online seller. Never act on one signal. Every state change needs two agreeing signals, and every hide is reviewed.
sweeps.expected_yield: 17 public rows today (4 confirmed); build guards for about 37 contradictory rows across the whole directory
sweeps.effort: 4 h build + 1 h review

sweeps.name: 4. Moved-shop check from the shop's own site and chain feeds
sweeps.fixes: Addresses out of date; feeds better addresses to sweep 2
sweeps.method: From the hours-sweep evidence, take single-location sites that pass hoursSweep's rule that the site names the shop, excluding platforms and chain headquarters. Compare the schema.org PostalAddress, or a printed address, with ours by house number and street. Flag when the street or house number differs by more than 2 numbers and more than 100 m, and the site's address is in the same city or ZIP. For WPSL chains (Wild Bill's, Sweet Fire, JO Cigars), take the feed's address and coordinates for each matching branch, and flag pins more than 250 m from the feed where the feed's address equals ours. Output decisions for review. Apply writes address, city and ZIP, then pin and zone (through sweep 2), keeping prev_address.
sweeps.sources: hours_evidence*.jsonl, render_*.jsonl, chain_evidence_wpsl.jsonl, plus the feeds' coordinates
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk: The site shows an office or warehouse address, or a sister branch (3 D's Cigars Pueblo vs Colorado Springs; Cigar Club Beaumont vs Lake Charles). Guardrails: the site must name this shop, single location only, same town, and every decision reviewed; the volume is small.
sweeps.expected_yield: About 9 now (1 confirmed: Kirsten), 60-110 if extended to printed addresses on all 3,616 working sites; 2-6 chain pins
sweeps.effort: Half a day (reuses the collected evidence)

sweeps.name: 5. City, ZIP and address text cleanup
sweeps.fixes: City-name problems; missing and junk addresses and ZIPs
sweeps.method: Expand USPS abbreviations to the GeoNames postal city for the ZIP ('Wshngtn Ct Hs' becomes Washington Court House). Restore capitals from Census names, and fix titleCase in buildDirectory and osm.js to keep Mc, Mac, De, La, O' and hyphenated parts. Replace county names with the postal city of the ZIP or pin, and change fillMissingCities to reverse-geocode at zoom 14 or finer with no county fallback. Canonicalize to one spelling per state and normalized name (St. Louis). Show the postal city for townships while search matches both (owner decision). Fill the 266 missing ZIPs from the ZIP area containing the pin (Census ZCTA shapes) or the geocoder's matched ZIP; clear malformed ZIPs. Trim and collapse whitespace (213). Move landmark prefixes ('Behind Outback Steakhouse, ...') into a note so the address starts with the street number (about 45). Blank the non-addresses ('TBD', 'Spinx', 'I-75', 'If You Don't Know...'; about 30) so the card shows the town and Directions searches by name. Send the 268 listings with no address, phone or website to the closure/storefront review; don't invent addresses for them.
sweeps.sources: GeoNames US postal codes, Census place, county-subdivision and ZCTA files, existing fields
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Decision: display the postal city ('Utica') or the legal municipality ('Shelby Twp')
sweeps.risk: Low; this is presentation and search. Guardrail: only replace a city that is a county, an abbreviation or a casing variant, never swap one real town for another; never touch owner-set rows.
sweeps.expected_yield: About 260 city fixes, about 270 ZIP fills or corrections, about 290 address strings cleaned
sweeps.effort: Half a day

audits.already_covered:
- **Pins are good for the vast majority:** median 56 m from their own address, 97.7% of geocodable listings within 1 km, and no systematic snapping to city centres. Every public row has lat/lng, state, city and a timezone.
- **State assignment:** geo.js snaps piers and barrier islands to a state and has the DC/Alexandria rule (12/12 tests). But the OSM file was fetched before that fix and never re-fetched, so 40542 still says Alexandria, DC.
- **Time zones:** fillTimezones covers every listing, and the zones are right for 7,400 of 7,431 (99.6%). The errors are all at the split-state lines.
- **Missing cities:** fillMissingCities already filled every blank public city (0 left), but it is also where the 35 county names came from.
- **Duplicates:** dedupeListings (same name and city within 200 m or same street) and the hidden 34 same-address duplicates are in place, as is the addressKey fix for Ste/Unit/Apt.
- **Chains:** chainCheck covers which branches a chain still has, not where their pins sit.
- **Directions:** the StoreProfile button already uses the address text rather than the pin, so a bad pin does not break it (a bad address or state still does).
- **Out-of-country data:** Overture was filtered to US/PR, so no Cuban, Bahamian or Mexican places leak in. The tz scan found only Windsor, Ontario, and one Lebanese record among public listings.

No existing job checks whether a pin, address, ZIP, state or timezone is correct. This whole area is new work.
audits.open_questions:
1. **Display name for township shops.** Show the postal city ("Utica") or the legal municipality ("Shelby Twp", 122 listings)? Mason's call.
2. **Foreign and self-contradicting records.** Hide or try to repair them: Windsor, Ontario; the Lebanese "Tobacco Bar"; Cigar Crafted and Cigar Vibes (Salt Lake City address, Houston pins, t-shirt-store websites); Mort's; Vip smoke; "Cigars" with ZIP 99931?
3. **The unverifiable listings.** About 875 listings can't be checked by free geocoders (311 with no address, 524 the Census couldn't match, 40 ties). Only Google Places would give authoritative coordinates and addresses for them. That needs an API key with billing, and its terms limit caching, so it suits a lookup when a listing is viewed rather than a bulk fix. Worth it?
4. **Hidden rows.** Should the same checks run over the 35,000 hidden rows before anyone un-hides from the admin queue? Across all rows there are 37 ZIP-prefix/state contradictions and 269 pins more than 25 km from their own ZIP.
5. **Hand-offs to other audits:**
   - 55 no-address OSM listings sit within 150 m of an addressed listing and are probably duplicates (dedupe audit).
   - Sam Hill's (10839): Yelp shows it CLOSED and samhillcigars.com is now a gambling site (closure and website audits).
   - Puro Estilo (20757) is an online seller (storefront audit).
6. **Watford City ND (31483).** The time-zone lookup says Mountain; the stored zone is Central, which I believe is correct. I left it out of the count and it needs a check.
7. **Sampling limits.** My verification covered 26 external lookups. The 100-130 pin estimate rests on 11 of 11 street-address cases and the 78-store chain calibration; highway-address cases were not sampled beyond the chain feed.

problems.title: Corrections don't stick, and edited websites aren't re-checked
problems.affected_public: 0 listings are harmed today (no public listing is claimed and 2 are staff-edited). But every phone or website fix to the 7,431 unclaimed listings is at risk on the next import.

examples: importStores.js line 112 runs 'phone = COALESCE(?, phone)' with no staff_edited guard, so any corrected phone on an unclaimed listing is overwritten by the next directory import.
The website survives an import only when staff_edited=1, which also freezes store_type and visibility.

An owner's PUT /stores/:id writes a new website but keeps the old website_status and website_final_url. A new working site stays hidden up to 30 days if the old one was dead. If the old one redirected, websiteInfo() sends visitors to the old destination, because 'moved' compares against the stale final URL.

Staff have no phone or website editor. The Links queue shows only non-ok statuses, so every problem above (all 'ok' or 'blocked') is invisible there. A 'wrong_info' report can only be closed or hidden.
problems.customer_impact: Fixes quietly revert, and a shop owner who corrects their site can end up linked to the old, wrong place.

sweeps.name: Link identity pass (extend linkCheck)
sweeps.fixes: Links that forward to gambling/spam/unrelated sites; parked and for-sale domains passing as working
sweeps.method:
Re-check all 3,540 shown links (force with recheck-days 0). Three new verdicts:

(1) Cross-domain redirect. When the final registrable domain differs from the listed one, call it 'same business' only if the destination names the shop: a distinctive name token (4+ letters, not generic, not the town) in <title>, og:site_name or JSON-LD name, or our phone digits, or our street number plus street word on the page. Otherwise the verdict is 'elsewhere'.

(2) Hijack. The title or first 64 KB contains at least 2 of: slot, gacor, togel, toto, judi, casino, bet88, sbobet, pragmatic, maxwin, 4d, game bai, doi thuong. The page must have no cigar or tobacco word. Verdict 'hijacked'.

(3) Parking. Any of:
- a body of 2 KB or less containing window.location.href="/lander" or a meta refresh to /lander;
- a final host of forsale.godaddy.com, expireddomains.com, dropcatch.com, domainmanage.com, *.gen.xyz, nomorewebsite.com, website-creator.org, afternic, sedo, dan.com or hugedomains;
- a title matching '^<domain> - <domain> Resources and Information'.
Verdict 'parked'.

Write only website_status and website_final_url. Keep the website value so a later re-check can restore it. Change websiteInfo() to follow website_final_url only on an explicit 'ok' same-business verdict, and to treat the three new statuses as dead. Give closureCheck parked or hijacked own-domain links as a weak 'likely_closed' signal, queued for staff and never auto-hidden. Output a dry-run decisions file, review it, then apply --from reviewed --confirm, as with hoursSweep.
sweeps.sources: The shop websites themselves (live fetch, same UA and limits as linkCheck), plus the existing website_final_url and today's crawl evidence to seed the review list.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing (one decision: whether a parked own-domain should enter the closure queue)
sweeps.expected_yield: About 70 hijacked or unrelated redirects, 9 for-sale redirects and 15 Google/login redirects hidden, plus the 83 parked links already evidenced. A further estimated 50-150 parked among the 564 thin 'ok' pages. Roughly 180-300 bad links gone.
sweeps.effort: About 1 day to build with self-tests from the confirmed examples (puffnstuffcigars.com, paradisecigars.com, greenestreetcigarcompany.net, lkblaw.com), 30 minutes to run, about 2 hours to review about 300 rows.

sweeps.risk: A real shop whose name appears only as a logo image, with no phone or address in text, could fail. Guards: logo alt text and og:site_name count; any phone or address match passes; the host-venue rule covers casinos and hotels (Mohegan Sun 22490, Caesars 9495/9496, La Quinta Resort 4781/4782); human review of every FAIL; claimed listings are never touched. The desk sample shows about 14 in 60 flagged rows are right, so review is mandatory, never auto-apply.

If it is ok and passes the identity check, and the site is single-location, store the root as the website. If the path is a chain branch page (/locations/, /stores/, a store-locator URL), don't fall back: send it to chainCheck as a possible closed branch (Wild Bill's Rogers City 17345, Roseville 19340).

sweeps.name: Phone checks: invalid, pin conflict, toll-free, shared and site-vs-listing
sweeps.fixes: Placeholder and foreign numbers; area code agreeing with ZIP but not state; toll-free lines; one number on many doors; our phone differing from the shop's site
sweeps.method:
PREREQUISITE: add a phone_source column ('website' | 'staff' | 'owner') and make importStores.js keep the phone when it is set. Today line 112 overwrites every phone, staff-edited ones included.

E1 Invalid. Match 555-55xx, 999-999-9999, repeated digits, a 0 or 1 at the start of the exchange, non-NANP country codes, and NANP codes outside the US and territories (for example 519, 809 outside PR). Clear the phone, or send foreign listings to address review. 5-7 rows.

E2 Pin conflict. Area-code state equals ZIP-prefix state but differs from the listing's state. Send to the address/pin review queue and never edit the phone. 9 rows: 22498, 24935, 10839, 5577, 42371, ...

E3 Toll-free. Send all 92 to storefront review (manufacturer, online-only, HQ, event, nonprofit). For real stores, look for a local number: the OSM twin phone, the chain's store page for this address (JSON-LD telephone), or a tel: link on a site page that names this street.

E4 Shared numbers. Same brand at different addresses: use the OSM twin or store-page number where one exists (Tobacco Hut: 4 via OSM), otherwise keep it, since it reaches the business. Different names at different addresses (50 groups): put the pair side by side in review. The listing whose own site shows the number keeps it; the other is cleared.

E5 Site phone. For single-location sites that pass the identity check, read JSON-LD telephone and tel: hrefs only, ignoring numbers labelled fax, text or events. If the site shows exactly one such number and ours appears nowhere on the site, propose a replacement with phone_source='website'. 89 candidates today.
sweeps.sources: The stored phone, osm_stores.json, shop websites (live), chain store-locator feeds and a ZIP3/area-code table (free).
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Nothing for E1-E5. Only a paid carrier lookup can tell whether a number is still in service: Twilio Lookup line type is about $0.008 per number, about $55 for all 6,664. Google Places Details also works, called when a listing is viewed (the closure plan already considers it). That needs Mason's API key and budget.
sweeps.risk: Fax numbers, second locations and an owner's cell number could replace the right number. The Tinder Box Dublin false alarm shows it. Guards: tel: and markup only, the single-number rule, our number must be absent from the whole site, never overwrite claimed or owner phones, and review every replacement. For E3 and E4, nothing is hidden automatically.
sweeps.expected_yield: 5-7 fake or foreign numbers cleared, 9 mislocated listings routed to address review, about 20-25 non-shops routed to storefront review, 4+ Tobacco Hut local numbers, and about 30-60 corrected phones from shop sites (Sunset Cigar Lounge 9589 first).
sweeps.effort: About 1 day plus the importer change, then 2-3 hours to review.

sweeps.name: Contact-field guardrails in code (not a data sweep)

sweeps.method:
Changes:
(1) In PUT /stores/:id and in importStores.js, when the website value changes, set website_status, website_final_url and website_checked_at to NULL and call checkStore(id) straight away.
(2) In websiteInfo(), render a NULL status as 'checking' (no link) rather than as ok, and follow website_final_url only on a same-business verdict.
(3) Add a staff editor for phone and website that writes phone_source or website_source='staff' without setting staff_edited.
(4) Make the Links queue list 'elsewhere', 'hijacked', 'parked', 'wrong_site' and platform links, not only dead ones.
(5) Label links with the registrable domain or the social network name.
(6) Drop the dead-domain sentence from the unclaimed banner, for consistency with hiding the link.
sweeps.sources: Code only: server/src/routes/stores.js, server/src/jobs/importStores.js, server/src/jobs/linkCheck.js, server/src/routes/admin.js, server/src/routes/links.js, client/src/pages/StoreProfile.jsx.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk: Small. Showing no link between an edit and its check hides a new site for a minute. Must keep the CRITICAL importer invariant: any field a sweep writes must be honoured by importStores.js.
sweeps.expected_yield: Every future fix from the sweeps above survives re-imports, and no visitor is sent to a stale redirect target.
