sweeps.name: S1 Record where each name came from, and stop the importer overwriting cleaned names (prerequisite)
sweeps.fixes: Makes every other name sweep durable. Gives staff name edits and a review queue that includes Overture rows.
sweeps.method:
Migration adds three columns:
- stores.source_name: the raw directory name, refreshed on every import.
- stores.name_source: 'directory' (default for all existing rows) | 'rule' | 'reviewed' | 'staff' | 'owner'.
- stores.name_aliases: a JSON array of former names, the legal name and the brand.

importStores.js always writes source_name. It writes name only when name_source is 'directory'. When name_source is 'rule', it re-applies the tidy function (S2) to the new source_name. When name_source is 'reviewed' and source_name has changed, it keeps the name and queues the row for review.

The owner PUT /stores/:id sets name_source to 'owner'. Add PATCH /admin/stores/:id/name, which sets 'staff' plus staff_edited = 1. Change /admin/listings to source IN ('osm','overture').

Prove it with the scratchpad test_reimport.js pattern: force a re-import on a scratch DB and assert that cleaned names survive. Extend the WORKLOG invariant: any sweep that changes a name must set name_source.
sweeps.sources: Existing code only.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk: None to shops. The one hazard is a wrong backfill; default every existing row to 'directory' so nothing changes until a sweep runs.
sweeps.expected_yield: Every later fix sticks. 6,887 Overture listings become reviewable in the admin queue.
sweeps.effort: 3-4 h build and test

sweeps.name: S2 Deterministic name tidy (display-only, reversible from source_name)
sweeps.fixes: Cosmetic formatting (about 290 names) and the damaged city casing (63 listings).
sweeps.method:
A pure function tidyName(source_name, ctx), run at import. Rules:
1. Collapse runs of spaces and the space before punctuation.
2. Strip a trailing ', LLC / Inc / Corp / Ltd / L.L.C.' only at the very end, and only if what remains still has a distinctive (non-trade) word. Never strip 'Co' or 'Company'. 'Tobacconist Llc' and 'Cigar Inc' stay. Keep the legal name in name_aliases.
3. Fix source casing damage: Llc to LLC, Usa to USA, and a lower-case word after '(' or '-'.
4. Strip '#NNN' (3+ digits) only when 2 or more other listings share the prefix or the website (Low Bob's, DOT Discount, Delaware Tobacco Outlet, Tobacco Barrel). Keep #1 to #99.
5. Casing, only for names that are fully upper or fully lower case. Take the shop's own og:site_name or schema.org name when it matches ignoring case and is mixed case. Otherwise use dictionary title-case with an acronym list, and send it to review, never auto-apply.
6. Never re-case a mixed-case name ('smooVe Cigars', 'BLEND Bar').

Skip any result that equals another listing's name in the same city.

In buildDirectory.js, fix titleCase() for Mc/Mac/O'/hyphenated towns (Winston-Salem, McKinney, O'Fallon).

Output: a decisions file of id, from, to and rule. Apply only a reviewed file with --from --confirm, as hoursSweep does.
sweeps.sources: The stores table. Schema.org names in hours_evidence*.jsonl. One fetch of the <head> for the 66 case rows.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk: A stylised brand spelling gets normalised, or a legal word that is part of the brand gets stripped ('Cigars Ltd' is a chain name, 'Pipes Ltd Cigar Hut'). Guards: only trailing legal words; mixed case is never touched; claimed, owner and staff rows are skipped; every case change is reviewed by a person; everything is reversible from source_name.
sweeps.expected_yield: About 182 legal suffixes, 66 case fixes, 19 store numbers, 16 casing artifacts, 12 whitespace fixes and 63 cities. The prototype output is work/clean_proposals.json.
sweeps.effort: 3 h build, 30 min review

sweeps.name: S3 Keyword-stuffing, marketing tails and status words (fully reviewed)
sweeps.fixes: Keyword and marketing names (about 31) and status words (6).
sweeps.method:
Flag a name when one of these holds:
- a separator (' - ', ' | ', ': ', '(...)') is followed by marketing words (best, voted, finest, newest, #1, % off, deliver, since, award);
- a separator is followed by 2+ product words (vape, CBD, kratom, delta 8, THC, hookah, glass, perfume, gifts, phones, slots, fireworks);
- the name contains 3+ product words anywhere.

Propose the text before the separator, and confirm it against the site's og:site_name or <title> when there is a site (Uhle's gives 'Uhle Tobacco Company').

Status words are routed, never just deleted:
- '(Coming Soon)' goes to the storefront/closure queue as not yet open.
- 'No Public Sales' becomes storefront = not_retail.
- '(members Only)' becomes a kept members-only note, reviewed.
- 'formerly X' moves X into name_aliases.

Branch suffixes ('- Fort Lauderdale', '(Durham)') stay.
sweeps.sources: Names plus the shop's own site title.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk: Cutting off part of a real name: 'Cigar Box Tobacconist and Vape Center' is the business name. Guards: the tail must match the word lists, the remainder must keep a distinctive word, and a person reviews all of about 40 rows.
sweeps.expected_yield: About 31 renamed. #41184 hidden as a not-yet-open pin, #16174 marked not retail, 3 'formerly' names become searchable aliases.
sweeps.effort: 2 h build, 20 min review

sweeps.name: S4 Rebrands and parent-company names, from each chain's own store list
sweeps.fixes: The Cheap Tobacco rebrand, the parent-company names, and the redirect-based rebrand candidates.
sweeps.method:
1. **Find candidates:** listings whose website redirects to a different, real business domain (linkCheck already stores website_final_url; exclude platforms and parked or spam targets). Today that is cheaptobaccousa.com (32 listings) plus about 12 others.
2. **Match against the chain's published list:** WP Store Locator feed or locations pages (chain_evidence_wpsl.jsonl plus a fresh fetch of /locations-list/). The town is always required. Same street number: propose. Same street, different number, or town only: review.
3. **Name:** use the brand name the chain's other listings already carry ('Wild Bill's Tobacco', as on 199 listings); the card already shows the town. Put the old name in name_aliases and set name_source = 'reviewed'.
4. **Duplicates first:** run the dedupe check before renaming and hide the duplicate (#41902 against #18968).
5. **No match, no rename:** acquired stores that are not on the chain's list (about 20 Cheap Tobacco, in 15 towns) go to the closure review, not a guessed rename.
6. **Parent names:** the same logic applies where the chain's store list names a different storefront at our address (Carrot Top Corporation becomes Cigaret Shopper; JO Cigars at Cape Coral becomes Habanos's Smoke Shop).
sweeps.sources: chain_evidence_wpsl.jsonl, the chains' locator pages, and website_final_url from linkCheck.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: One decision: show chain stores by brand only ('Wild Bill's Tobacco'), which I recommend, or brand plus town ('Wild Bill's of Greenville').
sweeps.risk: Renaming an independent shop that happens to share an address key, the '1060 Main St in another town' trap seen in the hours sweep. Guards: same town and same street number required; never rename on name similarity alone; claimed and staff rows are excluded; only a reviewed decisions file is applied.
sweeps.expected_yield: 13 Cheap Tobacco listings renamed (Akron after review). 1 duplicate hidden. About 20 sent to closure review. 2 parent-name fixes. About 5 to 10 further rebrands from the redirect list after review.
sweeps.effort: 3 h build, 30 min review

sweeps.name: S5 Recover the real name behind category-only names from the shop's own site
sweeps.fixes: Category-only names (255), plus the no-trade-word names that are registry or legal names.
sweeps.method:
For listings with a working site, read og:site_name, the first segment of <title>, the schema.org LocalBusiness name and the logo alt text. Accept a candidate only when all four hold:
1. The page passes the hours sweep's 'this site names this shop' test: it shows our street number, phone or town.
2. The candidate is not a platform, template or spam string (Linktree, My Blog, fujipub, SLOT777 and the like).
3. The candidate is not the parent retailer, unless the parent publishes this address. Brookshire Brothers' markup must not overwrite 'Tobacco Barn'.
4. The candidate is a specific name, not more category words.

When the site confirms the category name is the brand (Tobacco Depot, The Tobacco Shoppe, The Cigar Shop), leave it. For the 127 with no site, take the name of the OSM twin where one exists. Everything else stays until an owner claims the listing or a paid lookup is approved.
sweeps.sources: The shop's own site (a new collect pass over the <head>) and OSM names.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Only for the leftover 127 with no website: approval for Google Places displayName on view (paid; the terms limit storage to about 30 days). Otherwise nothing.
sweeps.risk: Taking the name of a wrongly linked site (fujipub.com, ametek.com, usps.com). Guard: the page must carry our street number or phone, and every rename is reviewed.
sweeps.expected_yield: An estimated 30 to 60 of the 86 with working sites get a specific name (6 of the 10 inspected had one). The rest are confirmed as genuine brands.
sweeps.effort: 3 h build, 25 min crawl, 30 min review

sweeps.name: S6 Send listings whose names say 'not a shop' (and joke places) to the storefront queue
sweeps.fixes: Names that say the place is not a shop, the co/company/house loophole (81 listings), and the private or joke places.
sweeps.method:
**Candidate words in the name:**
- HQ / headquarters / '(h Q)', union local, association, division / department / 'State of', trail / parking area, historic / buildings / landmark, research group, leaf tobacco dealer, 'No Public Sales', 'Worldwide HQ'.
- Known manufacturers: R.J. Reynolds, Lorillard, Swedish Match, General Cigar, Scandinavian Tobacco Group, Imperial, Universal Leaf, National Tobacco Co, Starbuzz, Blunt Wrap.
- Event, roller and mobile-service names.

**Combined with** the Overture category: corporate_office, tobacco_company, landmark_and_historical_building, coworking_space, hiking_trail, central_government_office, party_and_event_planning, wholesaler.

**Humidor sellers:** a humidor-named listing whose site is a humidor web catalogue is marked online_only.

**Loophole fix in storefrontCheck:** 'co', 'company' and 'house' no longer count as a premises word by themselves when the category is not retail. Those 81 go to review instead of staying.

**Private or joke places:** Meta source, no phone, no website, and either no street or a residential street with a possessive first name or words like home, porch, backyard, patio or shelter. These go to review with reason 'looks like a private place'.

Writes storefront plus storefront_reason, which the importer already honours.
sweeps.sources: Names, categories in overture_raw.json, and the humidor sellers' page titles.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: About 45 minutes of staff review for about 130 rows.
sweeps.risk: Hiding a factory that really sells retail (J.C. Newman's shop, Corona Cigar Co, Tampa factories). Guards: never auto-hide when the name also carries a shop word and the category is retail; a person reviews every row; hidden with a reason, never deleted.
sweeps.expected_yield: About 40 hidden with high confidence. About 25 event or mobile services decided. About 25 private or joke places reviewed. Probably 15 to 25 of the 81 loophole rows hidden.
sweeps.effort: 2 h build, 45 min review

sweeps.name: S7 Tags and feature flags from evidence, not from the name
sweeps.fixes: Walk-in Humidor, Pipes and Lounge tags and badges that nobody observed.
sweeps.method:
**Walk-in Humidor:** set only from the shop's own page text or schema.org amenityFeature (walk[- ]?in (cedar )?humidor | humidor room), OSM humidor=yes, or the owner. Extend hoursSweep's collect step to keep feature lines, not just hours lines. Drop the flag that comes only from the name; where the site is silent, show it as unknown, never as a 'no'.

**Pipes:** only from tobacco-pipe evidence (pipe tobacco, briar, meerschaum, pipe shop or tobacconist) in the name or on the site, extended to Overture names. Never when head-shop words are present (710, glass, water pipe, bong, dab, detox).

**Lounge:** stop deriving it from BrightQuery's cigar_bar category alone. Require lounge/bar/club/room words, a Meta/Foursquare/OSM lounge category, or site evidence. Exclude kava-only and vape-only names.

**Importer:** recompute tags on update for rows without owner or staff tags. Today tags are written on insert only, and has_* uses GREATEST, so it can never go down.
sweeps.sources: hours_evidence*.jsonl now (75 listings already found), a new collect pass, OSM tags.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk: Removing a true flag from a shop named 'The Humidor' that does have a walk-in. Guard: remove only when the site was readable and silent and the flag came from the name alone, and show 'unknown' rather than 'no'. Lounge-badge removals on about 300 BrightQuery rows are reviewed.
sweeps.expected_yield: Walk-in Humidor moves from 80 name-derived flags to an estimated 400 to 900 evidence-based ones (75 already found in the narrow text collected so far). 3+ online sellers lose the tag. Pipes is fixed on about 9 head shops and added to 100+ pipe shops. Lounge badge reviewed on about 300 rows.
sweeps.effort: 4 h build, 25 min collect, 30 min review

sweeps.name: S8 Fold punctuation and accents in search, and search aliases too
sweeps.fixes: The search misses; also makes old names (rebrands, legal names) findable.
sweeps.method: In GET /stores, match normalised text on both sides: lower-case, strip ’ ' ‘ ` and periods, fold accents (unaccent, or translate() if PGlite lacks the extension), treat & as 'and', and fold St/Saint and Mt/Mount for cities. Better: a name_search column maintained on import and edit from name plus name_aliases plus brand.
sweeps.sources: Code only.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk: None; this only affects search.
sweeps.expected_yield: 'wild bills' goes from 2 to 215 results, 'smokin joes' from 0 to 18, 'holts' from 0 to 3, 'low bobs' from 3 to 23. Former names like 'Cheap Tobacco' still find the renamed stores.

audits.already_covered:
- **Store type from the name:** storefrontCheck.js already hides wholesalers, distributors, importers, factories, museums, corporate/holding-company names, online-store names, Bitcoin ATMs and brewery/barbershop names that never name a cigar room of their own. That removed 537, and the importer honours it. S6 only adds vocabulary and the co/company/house fix; it does not redo this.
- **Duplicates:** dedupeListings.js and osm.nameKey/namesMatch already ignore the/inc/llc/co/company and generic trade words when matching duplicates, so duplicate detection does not depend on names being clean.
- **Wrong website links:** hoursSweep refuses sites that never name the shop (about 380 listings); that check can be reused as the guard in S5.
- **Chain branches:** chainCheck.js checks whether chain branches exist and replays reviewed decisions (apply --from --confirm); S4 reuses that pattern and its data.
- **Redirects:** linkCheck.js already records website_final_url, the free rebrand signal S4 uses.
- **Owner names:** claimed rows are never touched by the importer.
- **Descriptions:** the StoreProfile About card is hidden when there is no description, and the owner dashboard nudges owners to write one. Blank is handled correctly.
- **Card fallback:** the card monogram copes with any name.
- **Cigar search:** the cigar search is already accent- and case-insensitive per word (WORKLOG). Only the store search lacks this.
audits.open_questions:
1. **Chain name format (your call).** Show the brand ('Wild Bill's Tobacco') or the chain's branch label ('Wild Bill's of Greenville')? I recommend the brand, since the card already shows the street and town.
2. **Small branch numbers.** Keep the #1 to #14 numbers some chains use publicly ('Tobacco House #6')? I recommend keeping them and stripping only 3+ digit internal codes.
3. **Legal names.** Show the trading name and keep the legal name only as a searchable alias? I recommend yes.
4. **Descriptions.** I recommend leaving them blank until an owner writes one. Do not generate them, and do not pull meta descriptions from sites: 16 linked shop domains now serve gambling spam.
5. **Paid lookup.** Is Google Places displayName on view acceptable for the 127 category-only names with no website? Only a paid source fixes those reliably.
6. **Joke and private places.** Hide the private and joke 'lounges' on staff review, or also require the closure sweep's signals?
7. **Hand-offs to other areas (found while auditing names):**

sweeps.name: 2. Website amenity sweep (lounge, walk-in humidor, BYOB, bar, lockers, members-only, drive-thru, patio)
sweeps.fixes: Problems 1, 2, 3 and 4 for listings with a working site
sweeps.method:
COLLECT
- Extend hoursSweep.collectOne instead of crawling again. Add lounge|member|amenit|about|faq|our-shop to LINK_HINT and keep up to 4 pages. Besides the hours snippets, keep 'amenity snippets': any line matching the vocabulary below, with 1 line of context either side, and the question line before any answer.
- Keep JSON-LD name, description, amenityFeature and @type (BarOrPub, NightClub) only from business nodes. Drop Article, BlogPosting, Product, Event, Breadcrumb and ImageObject nodes, and pages under /blog, /news, /product, /events.
- Re-run hoursRender for script-drawn sites.

DECIDE (per amenity)
Lounge, positive: cigar lounge, smoking lounge, our lounge, lounge hours, lounge seating, shop & lounge, cigar bar, smoking room, relax in our lounge, or a 'Yes' answer to a lounge FAQ question.
Lounge, negative: no lounge, retail only, carry-out only, 'we do not have a lounge', lounge closed.
Access: members-only, private club, membership required, lounge membership, 'open to the public', 24/7 member access.
Walk-in humidor: /walk[\s-]*in humidor/, 'humidor room', or 'N sq ft humidor'.
BYOB: BYOB or 'bring your own beverage/bottle'. Conditional forms ('only during ticketed events', Ol' Havana #9449) mean no.
Bar: full bar, liquor license, cocktails, beer & wine served on site.
Lockers: cigar, humidor, member or private lockers.
Drive-thru: only in a sentence about this shop, e.g. 'This location offers a convenient Drive-Thru window!' (Tobacco House #7124) or HTX Cigars' 'drive-through humidor'.
Patio: patio, fire pit, outdoor lounge.
Mobile service: 'mobile lounge', 'we bring the smoke to you', 'book us for your event'. This flags the listing for storefront review; it is not a lounge.

GUARDRAILS (all have real triggers in today's data)
- Only the shop's own site: reuse NOT_THE_SHOPS_SITE and mentionsShop(). Tobacco Barn links Brookshire Brothers grocery pages, whose 'Pharmacy Drive-Thru' matched 12 times; #13031 in Iowa links the Ridgewood NJ shop's site.
- A shared site binds a statement to a branch only by address, town or phone. Reuse the text-at-address anchoring and chainCheck.addressKey: 'Davidus Cigars Olney ... massive cigar lounge' must not badge 11 other Davidus stores, and 'C.B. Perkins Hyannis Cigar Lounge' must not badge Canton or Falmouth. A chain-wide sentence applies to all branches only when it says each or all ('Each of our retail stores walk-in humidor', Smoke Inn).
- Disqualify:
  - future or construction wording ('build our dream cigar lounge', Fairway #2085)
  - another business ('Visit our friends at Smoke Rings Cigar Bar', Cigar Box PA)
  - trade-show or blog titles ('Inside the Lounge: Konscious Cigars at PCA 2023')
  - notices older than about 18 months, or COVID notices (Humidor Palm Coast #6347)
  - Wild Bill's-style navigation or template text that appears on every branch page
- Decisions:
  - add: at least 1 positive and no negative
  - remove: an explicit negative, or, for category-only badges, a site read with 3 or more pages of real text and no lounge vocabulary. That result is 'not confirmed' and goes to review; it never becomes an automatic false.
  - Never override a lounge claim made by the name without an explicit negative.
  - Skip claimed, owner-set and staff-set listings.
- Write decisions and skip reasons, have reviewers check about 60 decisions against the live sites (split between adds and removes), turn each miss into a rule and a selftest, then apply --from --confirm. Store the quote and URL as provenance, and show 'from the shop's website' on the profile.
sweeps.sources: Shop websites, reusing hoursSweep collect and hoursRender, the chain evidence files, and the existing hours evidence for a first pass
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Decisions: (1) show a 'Members only' / 'Private club' qualifier next to Lounge; (2) which amenity chips to show (I suggest Lounge, Walk-in humidor, BYOB, Bar, Lockers). No keys or money; puppeteer-core stays local, as today.
sweeps.risk:
The main false-positive paths are all observed in today's evidence: a sister branch's lounge credited to every branch, blog or template text, FAQ questions, and another business's page. A false add sends someone to a counter with no seats. Guardrails:
- the branch binding and disqualifiers above
- the review rounds
- a 'not confirmed' state instead of false
- provenance shown on the page
- apply only a reviewed file.
Never hides a listing.
sweeps.expected_yield: From the existing capture alone: about 68 lounge adds on single-listing sites, about 40-60 more after branch binding on 37 shared sites, about 78 walk-in humidor adds, about 48 members-only qualifiers, 10 BYOB, about 55 lockers. After a full re-read: an estimated 300-450 lounge adds, several hundred walk-in humidors, and about 100-120 of the 137 category-only badges on sites resolved (mostly to 'not confirmed').
sweeps.effort: About 1.5-2 days to build (snippet capture, decide rules and selftests, provenance UI). The crawl reuses the ~25-minute collect plus the ~1-hour render. Review: 2 rounds of about 60 decisions, 3-4 hours.

sweeps.name: Hours logic and parser fixes, map hours re-derived from source
sweeps.fixes: Two-range day values, OSM tails, site typos and misreads, extended times over 24:00
sweeps.method: (1) parseRange and openStatus evaluate every comma-separated range, not just the first. (2) osmRange: a leading 00:00-0X:00 segment (X at most 4) becomes the previous day's close, never part of a 24-hour day; accept 25:00-28:00. (3) normText: '12: 00 am' becomes '12:00am'. In sane(), '4 pm - 12 pm' with the close exactly 12pm and an evening open means midnight, not a flipped opening. (4) A plausibility rule at decide time: a day whose opening or closing is 12 hours off the shop's other days (at least 2 others agreeing), a span under 2 hours, or an opening between 12:01am and 4:59am with an afternoon close. That day becomes unknown and goes to the review file; auto-flip am/pm only when the flip matches the other days exactly. (5) buildDirectory re-parses hours_raw with the current converter instead of copying fetch-time hours, and the importer runs the same parse. Write: corrected hours for the 8 flagged listings after review; map rows re-derived on the next build.
sweeps.sources: Existing stored hours, hours_raw, captured site lines; no new fetches
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk: A genuinely short or odd day (a 2-hour Sunday) becomes unknown, which is never shown as Closed, so it is harmless. Guardrail: extend the parser self-tests with every example above; diff all 1,301 directory records before and after (expect about 173 changes) and review the ones that gain a Closed day or become 24 hours.
sweeps.expected_yield: 4 split-value listings fixed (Euphoria correct all week); 6-8 typo days made unknown or corrected; no regression for Tailored Smoke and 3 others
sweeps.effort: 4-6 h including tests

sweeps.name: Freshness cadence with season windows
sweeps.fixes: Seasonal schedules, no freshness or provenance, holiday badges, stale map rows
sweeps.method: (1) Parse date windows ('Winter Hours Oct 1st - June 20th', 'July/August', 'BEGINNING 9/14', 'Summer hours') into hours_valid_from and hours_valid_until. Refuse a schedule whose window excludes today, and schedule a re-check at the boundary. (2) A monthly re-collect of all website-sourced listings (about 25 minutes) plus decide. Auto-apply only when the new reading equals the stored one, or when two consecutive runs agree; any change goes to a review queue. Weekly for the 19 seasonal ones, for lounges (cigar shops and lounges were 26-29% badly wrong in the overlap, tobacco shops 7%), and for any listing with views or follows. sweeps.name: thumbCheck: vet every thumbnail (load, content, contrast, duplicates, deny-list)
sweeps.fixes: Placeholders/icons/stock, invisible logos, the chain-photo decision, broken images, and the takeover pictures caught by URL (marketplaces, dummy.png)
sweeps.method:
A new job staged like hoursSweep (collect, decide, review, apply --from reviewed file --confirm).

collect: GET each web_image_url with browser headers and no Referer; retry the 403s in the headless Chrome pass (7 of 883 URLs load only in Chrome). Record status, content type, bytes, pixel size, alpha, a perceptual hash, and the visible share on the rendered 72 px card for both backgrounds.

decide:
(a) Drop anything that is not an image, fails to decode, or is under 120 px on its short side.
(b) Drop on a URL deny-list: domain marketplaces (domainmarket, expireddomains, hugedomains, sedo, afternic, dan.com, porkbun/l.ink); builder defaults (editmysite app/marketing og_image and og-image-placeholder, lovable.dev/opengraph-image, og-image.spri.ng, /sample-website-media/); theme demo files (dummy, placeholder, neve-*logo, web-agency-logo); favicon, fav-icon, apple-touch-icon, divider, spacer, warning, arrow and star strips; stock (wsimg isteam/getty and isteam/stock, images.unsplash.com, pexels-, gettyimages-, shutterstock); Wix library media (a 32-hex filename with no owner prefix); ebayimg, bonfireassets and yimg. Send vimeocdn and favicons over 150 px to review rather than dropping them.
(c) If the visible share is under 4% on the background the card would use but at least 10% on the other, keep the picture and store web_image_bg = light or dark. If it is blank on both, drop it.
(d) The same perceptual hash under two or more unrelated website domains marks a platform default or stock photo: drop.
(e) An image on 3 or more listings at different addresses that is not a logo (no 'logo' in the URL, no transparency, not roughly square on a flat background) is a chain photo: apply the owner's chain policy (use the chain logo, or drop to the monogram).

apply: set web_image_url to NULL for drops, write web_image_bg, and stamp web_image_checked_at. Never touch claimed, staff_edited or owner-set rows, and re-check that at write time (the current image apply does not).
sweeps.sources: The existing web_image_url values, the image files themselves, and headless Chrome (already used by hoursRender.js). No external API.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: One decision: the chain policy for the 232 branch-photo and 93 banner listings (the chain logo on every branch, the monogram, or keep the banner). A new web_image_bg column (a schema migration). Nothing else.
sweeps.risk: A false drop only turns a real shop's picture back into the monogram. It never changes a fact or hides a shop, so the downside is small. Guardrail: render every drop and background change onto a contact sheet (the sheet.py approach: 853 images in 15 sheets reviewed in minutes) and apply only the reviewed file. Soft signals (Vimeo frames, large favicons, casino-resort images) go to review, never to automatic drops.
sweeps.expected_yield: About 110-130 pictures dropped (the 58 placeholders, icons and stock, the 32 broken, the invisible ones with no usable background, and the 4 marketplace images), about 25-40 logos rescued by the right background, and 232-325 chain images replaced or dropped depending on the policy.
sweeps.effort: Build 5-6 h; run about 15 min (883 URLs) plus a Chrome retry; review about 1 h of contact sheets.

sweeps.name: Picture identity gate: the page must name the shop, not just the domain
sweeps.fixes: Another organisation's website supplying the picture (Tobacco Master's hours too), and new takeover pictures on keyword-stuffed pages
sweeps.method:
In hoursSweep collect, also save <title>, og:title and og:site_name. In decide, allow a picture (and website hours) only when:
(1) the title, og:site_name or JSON-LD name contains a distinctive name word as a whole word, and the title, description or JSON-LD also carries a trade word (cigar, tobacco, tobacconist, smoke, pipe, humidor, lounge, vape, hookah); or
(2) the site's domain stem contains the whole distinctive name stem (mikescigarroom counts; groutmasters for 'Master', dreamforth for 'Dream' or arizonatrellis for 'Arizona' do not).

Names made only of generic words ('Tobacco Store', 'The Cigar Bar', 'The Cigar Shop') get no picture unless the domain is itself the name (e.g. thecigarshop*.com). Remove the fallback that re-admits town words when nothing else is left ('Forest Lake Tobacco' at forestlakechamber.org). Add local.yahoo.com, wikipedia.org and usps.com to NOT_THE_SHOPS_SITE. Re-run decide on the existing evidence, diff the result against what is applied, and review it.
sweeps.sources: The existing evidence JSONL plus a re-collect of titles (the ~25-minute collect already fetches these homepages).
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk: A real shop whose page title is only a slogan could lose its picture, and possibly its website hours if the gate is also applied to hours. The cost is a monogram and 'Hours not listed', never a wrong fact. Review the diff of the listings that lose hours before applying; for pictures alone, drops can be automatic.
sweeps.expected_yield: Removes the 11 wrong-business pictures and Tobacco Master's grout-company hours, and stops the whole class from coming back. It probably catches a handful more among the 1,427 that the contact sheets left ambiguous.
sweeps.effort: 2-3 h build; collect about 25 min; decide in minutes; about 30 min review.

sweeps.name: Takeover and for-sale domain detector (with the link sweep)
sweeps.fixes: The 14 spam and for-sale pictures today, plus the same domains' website links and any website hours
sweeps.method:
For every public website (not only those with pictures), fetch the homepage title, og:title, og:image and final URL. Flag it as hijacked when:
- the title or og:title has gambling vocabulary (slot, gacor, togel, judi, situs, jackpot, 188bet, maxwin, casino with bet or slot), or a non-Latin script title (CJK, Thai, Vietnamese betting terms) for a US shop, or an og:image on another host whose path has those words, and in every case the title does not name the shop.

Flag it as parked when the title, final host or og:image says 'for sale', 'make an offer', 'a brand new domain', or points to expireddomains, domainmarket, hugedomains, sedo, afternic, dan.com or porkbun l.ink.

Write website_status = hijacked or parked; both count as dead, like today's 'parked'. Clear web_image_url and any website-sourced hours, and pass the listing to closureCheck's weak 'likely_closed' signal. Use a reviewed decisions file only.
sweeps.sources: Shop homepages (one GET each, like linkCheck); the existing evidence files for a head start.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing (optionally: whether a hijacked domain should also mark the listing likely_closed)
sweeps.risk: Lounges inside casino resorts mention 'casino' legitimately: 5222 Pivat at Agua Caliente, 9843 Skookum Creek at Little Creek, 6610 Gurkha at Hollywood Gulf Coast, 8747 Bear River Rancheria. Guard by requiring the vocabulary in the title and the shop's name absent from the title, and review every flag before applying. A false flag hides a real website link, which is recoverable, so review is enough.
sweeps.expected_yield: 14 confirmed listings with pictures (5765, 10190, 10839, 17595, 5721, 4309, 3623, 21088, 32538, 34423, 11671, 31609, 5249, 20144). A text scan found about 52 candidates across all collected sites; I expect roughly 15-30 more real hijacks after review.

sweeps.name: Cached, resized thumbnails served from our own domain
sweeps.fixes: Fragile hot-links, pictures swapped after review, multi-megabyte originals, cropped fragments
sweeps.method: After thumbCheck approves an image, download it once. Resize to a 160x160 WebP: a centre crop for photos; for logos and any image wider than 1.8:1, fit it inside the square on the computed background. Store it through utils/storage.js (R2 when S3_* is set) or, since each file is about 5-10 KB, in a small store_thumbs table served at /api/store-thumbs/:id with long cache headers. Keep the source URL and a hash. A monthly re-check fetches the source: if the hash changed or the site turned hijacked, parked or dead, re-vet it instead of silently updating. The resize can run locally like hoursRender.js, so the server gains no native dependency (sharp or Pillow runs on Mason's machine).
sweeps.sources: The vetted image URLs; utils/storage.js; the existing multer and storage code.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: A decision to re-host shops' share images (og:image is published for exactly this link-preview use; keep an opt-out). Either the S3_* keys for R2 (already on his list) or approval to keep about 10 MB of thumbnails in Postgres. A Railway local directory is wiped on deploy without a volume.
sweeps.risk: The main failure is caching a bad picture, which is why this runs only after thumbCheck and the identity gate. A caching bug would show monograms, not wrong facts. Guardrail: keep the source URL so a picture can be re-vetted or removed in one step.
sweeps.expected_yield: All of about 1,300 kept pictures load reliably, including the 2 blocked by CORP, the 5 that depend on no Referer, and TLS or http-only hosts such as JM Cigars' storefront photo. Average bytes per thumbnail drop from 316 KB to about 6 KB (about 50x lighter), and text banners are fitted rather than cut into fragments.
sweeps.effort: 4-6 h build; about 15 min run; monthly re-check about 10 min.

sweeps.name: Better free picture sources plus an owner upload, and client hardening
sweeps.fixes: Low coverage (only 19% of public listings have a picture), chain logos, owners unable to fix their own picture, the light/dark background guess
sweeps.method:
(1) From the evidence already collected, use schema.org 'logo' (924 public listings) and 'image' (703): prefer a square logo over a wide og:image share card, and fill gaps for the 2,113 listings with evidence but no thumbnail (235 have a logo, 243 an image). Pass everything through thumbCheck and the identity gate. Sweet Fire's own logo 'sft-logo-on-black.jpg' is there. Wild Bill's 'logo' field is really a cover photo, so apply the chain policy.
(2) Add apple-touch-icon (180 px square) to collect, with a hash deny-list for builder default icons.
(3) Build the missing owner upload for logo_url and cover_url on the claim dashboard (storage.js and multer exist), plus a staff 'remove picture' action in the admin Listings tab.
(4) In StoreThumb, use the server's web_image_bg instead of /logo/ in the URL; treat an image under 64 px on load as failed; fit very wide images inside the square instead of cropping.
(5) Do not bother with OSM: 9 image tags among 9,234 US tobacco objects (measured).
(6) Mapillary street-level photos (free token, CC BY-SA, attribution required) are possible only with human review, because a photo near the pin often shows the street, not the door.
sweeps.sources: The existing evidence JSONL; shop homepages (apple-touch-icon); owners; optionally the Mapillary API.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Nothing for (1), (2) and (4). For (3), a go-ahead to build the upload UI. For Mapillary, a free API token and a decision on attribution. Google Places Photos would give real storefront photos but is paid, the photos cannot be stored, and it needs a billing key and his decision.
sweeps.risk: A JSON-LD 'image' can be a product shot or a sister branch, so the same vetting and the chain rule apply, and new pictures go through the contact-sheet review. Owner uploads are authoritative and carry no false-positive risk. A client-side change affects only presentation.
sweeps.expected_yield: About 250-400 more listings with a usable picture from data already on disk, legible logos for about 25-60 listings that are blank or borderline today, and an owner path that makes every claimed shop's picture correct.
sweeps.effort: (1) 2 h; (2) a collect change of 1 h plus the re-collect run; (3) 4-6 h; (4) 1-2 h.

audits.already_covered:
Working well, so don't redo:

problems.title: The menu scanner is stuck re-reading the same failed shops, so no new shop is ever read and most current shelves will stop refreshing
problems.affected_public: Measured: 3,243 public listings with a working website have never been read. Projected by replaying the scanner on the snapshot: 36 of the 43 public shelves get no re-read in the next 30 days, and 0 never-read listings are reached.
problems.how_measured: scanStale() treats a store as due when it was never checked, was checked more than 7 days ago, or has menu_matcher_version IS DISTINCT FROM 4, and orders by claimed, confidence, id. syncStoreMenu writes the matcher version only after a successful read. So 323 public listings (208 unsupported, 113 errors, 2 no_products) keep a NULL version and are due on every scan. Replaying the ORDER BY on the snapshot: all of the next 60 picks are previously failed stores, and none is new. Production timestamps agree. The last boot scan (40 stores) re-read 875 first, then ids 24, 126, 186, 208, 223 ... 578 in id order, all unsupported or errors. A 30-day replay of the 6-hourly 60-store scans reaches no new listing and re-reads only 7 of the 43 shelves (414, 458, 501, 566, 593, 680, and the failing 875). A manual admin scan (limit 200 or less) uses the same order and would not help. scanStale also ignores website_status: 90 of the 113 errors are on links already known to be dead.
examples: 875 The Lord Of The Cigars: always first in the queue (synced before, version mismatch) and fails every 6 hours on the 2 MB cap. Confirmed from menu_status and timestamps.
24 Hawaii Cigar & Ukulele, 186 Padre Island Cigar Company, 208 Estate Cigars & Social: 'unsupported', re-read on every scan. Confirmed from timestamps.

sweeps.name: Unstick the menu scanner, skip dead links, and read every working site once (dry run first)
sweeps.fixes: Stuck scanner; feeds the shared-feed, expiry and brand-list sweeps
sweeps.method: Code changes in scanStale and syncStoreMenu: (1) record a reader version or attempt stamp on every outcome, and apply the matcher-version clause only to rows with menu_last_synced; (2) back off by outcome: ok re-read after 7 days, unsupported after 60 days, errors after 3, 7, 14, then 30 days (a fail count), and skip any website_status other than ok or blocked; (3) put never-read listings ahead of low-value re-reads. Before the first write for a shop never synced, require all of: the site names the shop (reuse hoursSweep's name check), the host is not shared with another public listing (otherwise route to the shared-feed sweep), storefront='yes', and operating_status not closed. One-time: a '--dry-run --all' pass over the 3,243 unread working sites (about 3 fetches each, 1.5 s pause) writes a review file of {store, platform, products, matched, brands, 10 sample lines}. Review 30 at random plus every shop with more than 500 matches, then apply only the reviewed file.
sweeps.sources: Shop websites (Shopify products.json, WooCommerce Store API), stores.website_status, hours_skips_final.json and hoursSweep's name matcher
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk: Importing a stranger's catalog through a mislinked website. Seen in passing: 3444 'House of Cigar & Tobacco' links cigar.com, 928 'Nick's Cigar' links perdomocigars.com, 2426 'Del Mar Wine & Cigar' links bytefederal.com. The name check, the shared-host rule and the dry-run review guard against this. A 60-day backoff can delay a shop that moves to Shopify, which is acceptable.
sweeps.expected_yield: 42 of the 395 public listings already read (10.6%) produced matched stock. Applied to the 1,529 unread listings that pass both guards, that is roughly 160 new public shelves, with a wide margin because the 395 are from FL, TX and CA only. More follow once the shared-feed sweep settles chains. Every existing shelf gets its weekly re-read back.
sweeps.effort: Code 2-3 h; crawl about 4 h unattended; review about 2 h

sweeps.name: Take hidden listings' stock and $0 prices out of public counts
sweeps.fixes: Hidden listings' stock counted on cards and in search; $0.00 prices on the cigar page
sweeps.method: (a) In cigars.js (list, /followed, the city/state, min/max price and in_stock_only filters, price-comparison), smoke-list.js and users.js, join stores and require s.visible = 1. Use MIN(NULLIF(i.price,0)) for min_price, and in /availability count a price only when it is > 0 (show 'price not listed' otherwise). (b) When storefrontCheck, closureCheck, dedupeListings, chainCheck or staff hide a listing, set its source='web' rows to in_stock=0 without deleting them; an unhide plus the next read restores them. One-time for the 4 hidden listings (2,790 rows). Test: for the 741 affected lines, store_count must equal /availability length; re-check Kristoff Sumatra (176) and Hoyo Excalibur (79).

sweeps.name: Expire web stock that has not been confirmed recently
sweeps.fixes: Stock never retired when a feed stops answering
sweeps.method: When a shop's last successful read (menu_last_synced) is older than N days (suggest 21), set its source='web' rows to in_stock=0 with an 'expired' marker, not deleted. Turn the 'checked N days ago' label amber after 7 days on both the store page and the cigar page. A successful read restores the rows. Run it inside scanStale so it needs no extra job.
sweeps.sources: Database only
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Choose the window (14, 21 or 30 days)
sweeps.risk: A shop whose site blocks our reader for 3 weeks loses a real shelf. That is honest, because we can no longer vouch for it; the label can read 'last seen on its site on DATE'.
sweeps.expected_yield: No row expires today. It stops indefinite staleness on all 43 shelves and every future one; 875 would expire first if it is not fixed.
sweeps.effort: About 2 h

sweeps.name: Attach a shared online store to the right branch
sweeps.fixes: One online store's stock at every listing sharing its website
sweeps.method: For a website shared by 2 or more public listings, reuse the chain stage's address matching (chainCheck, hoursSweep chains, WPSL feeds). If the site names exactly one address, attach its feed only to that listing (3J's: Lake Worth). The other listings get 'This company sells online at <site>' with a link and no stock. A listing whose site never names it (1369 '1804 Cigars Davie', 1954 '3js Cigar Boca') gets no stock and goes to the website-link review. For true multi-branch chains with one web store (Anthony's), follow the owner's rule: either attach to every branch with the label 'stock from the company's online store: call this location to confirm', or attach to the flagship only. Write a decisions file per group and apply only after review.
sweeps.sources: chain_evidence.jsonl, chain_evidence_wpsl.jsonl, hours_skips_final.json, shop sites
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Decide how a multi-branch chain's web stock is shown
sweeps.risk: A branch that really does carry the items loses its shelf; the link to the company's store keeps the path open. Only 4 groups exist today, so each can be reviewed by hand. The number grows once the scanner is unstuck, which is exactly why this sweep must come first for chains.
sweeps.expected_yield: Today 7 extra copies across 11 listings. Prevents about 1,449 chain listings (332 sites) from inheriting a web warehouse's stock.

sweeps.name: Complete WooCommerce and Shopify reads
sweeps.fixes: WooCommerce reader drops the brand and stops early
sweeps.method: WooCommerce: give matchCigar and buildCatalog a brand hint from (1) the Store API 'brands' field, (2) an attribute named Brand or pa_brand, or (3) a category whose name, minus 'Cigars', equals an established catalog brand. Never use a generic category (Cigar, Boutique, Maduro, Sale, Cuban). Paginate by X-WP-TotalPages (safety cap 60), use per_page=50, and raise MAX_BODY to 8 MB for JSON endpoints only. On a Store API 404, try /wp-json/wc/store/products, then the product sitemap plus Product JSON-LD. Shopify: paginate until an empty page (cap 40) rather than stopping at 8; record 402 'store unavailable' and 401 'password' as their own statuses and pass 402 to the link and closure checks. Before any production run, re-run the matcher offline on re-fetched Lake Worth and Grapevine feeds plus feeds_cache.json. Shopify matches must not change, and every new WooCommerce match must name a brand present in its category.
sweeps.sources: Shop websites; feeds_cache.json for the regression
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk: A category mistaken for a brand pins products to the wrong line. The established-brand rule and a review of 50 random new matches before applying guard against it.
sweeps.expected_yield: WooCommerce match rate from 61% toward Shopify's 92% across 20 shops (on the order of 2,000 more rows). Lake Worth's 704 unread products become readable. 875 is readable again, which clears its 16 retired-line rows.

sweeps.name: Shelf hygiene: non-cigar goods, non-brand labels, price plausibility
sweeps.fixes: Non-cigar goods and non-brand labels; implausible price
sweeps.method: Add to NOT_CIGAR: coffee, espresso, ground, caddy, telescopic, 'single cigar tube', scissors, multi tool, 'leather traveler', flask. Drop a product only when its title and URL also lack a size or ring gauge, so real cigars such as 'M by Macanudo Coffee and Espresso' and 'Cinco Estrellas Coffee' robusto survive. Retire (not delete) catalog lines whose brand is a non-brand ('Flavored', 'Vendor-unknown', '... Coffee', vendor phrases over 4 words). Re-file them under the shop's house brand when the vendor is the shop. Merge brand spellings within edit distance 1 of an established brand seen at 5 or more shops ('Aleck' to 'Alec') through a reviewed list. Price guard: parse the pack count (Single, 5-Pack, Box of 20). Flag a price per stick above $150 or below $0.50, or a box more than 3x the median box of that line at that shop; show 'price not listed' and queue it. Apply only a reviewed file.
sweeps.sources: Database, shop feeds
sweeps.needs_from_mason: nothing
sweeps.risk: Hiding a real cigar with an accessory-like name. The size-token rule and the reviewed list guard against it.
sweeps.expected_yield: Today: 24 non-cigar lines, about 103 mislabeled lines, 1 absurd price. It also stops these repeating as coverage widens.
sweeps.effort: 3-4 h plus 1 h review

sweeps.name: Brands carried, read from shop websites (no stock claim)
sweeps.fixes: Brand lists not captured; house-brand shops showing nothing
sweeps.method: Extend hoursSweep 'collect', which already fetches the homepage and up to 3 pages per site: keep visible text, nav and link text and image alt text, and follow one link matching /brands|cigar-brands|our-cigars|humidor|walk-in|selection/. Match established catalog brands, word-bounded; ambiguous names (Foundation, Protocol, Punch, Java, Acid, Warped, Asylum) count only when followed by 'Cigars'. Accept a page only when (a) 5 or more distinct brands appear in list context (li, nav or menu items, logo alts, or within 10 lines after a heading containing brand, carry, humidor or selection), (b) the page is not /blog/, /events/ or /news/ and not dated, (c) the site names the shop, and (d) for a chain-shared site, only the branch page counts. Write store_brands(store_id, brand, source='website', source_url, seen_at). For house-brand feeds (vendor is the shop, 0 matched), write the house brand with its product count. Show on the store page as 'Brands listed on its website (checked DATE)' with a link, never as 'in stock'. Review 50 random rows plus all chain rows before applying; refresh monthly alongside the hours collect.
sweeps.sources: Shop websites (already fetched by hoursSweep collect), catalog brands, feeds_cache.json
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Approve the wording, and decide whether unclaimed shops show it
sweeps.risk: Brands pulled from an event announcement, a blog post or a mislinked site (404 unread listings fail the name check). The list-context rule, the name check and the review sample guard against it. The label never implies stock.

audits.already_covered:
Already handled well, so the plan should not redo it:

- **The feed reader** (webMenu.js) is careful:
  - Shopify and WooCommerce feeds, refusal of private IPs, a single identifiable user agent, a 1.5 s pause between shops, and a body cap.
  - A cigar-vocabulary filter plus an accessory reject list.
  - Upserts keyed on external_id, with no duplicate rows found (row counts match matched counts).
  - Products that leave the feed are set to in_stock=0, not deleted. Owner-entered rows are never touched, and shops can opt out.
  - Unmatched titles go to catalog_pending. House-brand shops are not force-matched: Mr. Cigars, Soles and Serafin correctly get 0 matches.
- **The MATCHER_VERSION re-read worked.** About 70 shops were re-read on version 4 within hours, and only 16 public rows remain on retired lines. Those are at 875, which cannot be read.
- **The store page:**
  - It shows brand, then line, then sizes, with price ranges.
  - It drops $0 prices (NULLIF).
  - It labels web stock 'From the shop's site · checked X ago'.
- **"Where to find it"** filters to visible listings and labels the web source and its freshness.
- **Prices are overwhelmingly plausible.** One bad price in 12,306 in-stock sizes.
- **Nothing is stale today.** Every public shelf was confirmed within the last day.
- **Adjacent sweeps already in place, which the proposed sweeps reuse:**
  - linkCheck's website_status.
  - The hours sweep's 'site never names this shop' check (380 + 38 + 14 listings).
  - The chain address matching.

The missing pieces are:
- a scanner queue that moves;
- visibility filters on the cigar-list queries;
- expiry of unconfirmed stock;
- branch attribution for shared feeds;
- any capture of brand lists.
audits.open_questions:
Decisions only the owner can make, then things I noticed outside this area.

**Decisions**
1. **Chain web stores.** Should a chain's single online store (Anthony's x3, Miami Humidor x2, and later Corona Cigar x3 and Wild Bill's x201) show as stock at every branch with a 'call to confirm' label, at the flagship only, or only as a link?
2. **Expiry window** for unconfirmed web stock: 14, 21 or 30 days.
3. **Brand lists.** Should they show on unclaimed shops, and with what wording? I suggest 'Brands listed on its website (checked DATE)'.
4. **Large product crawls.** Is crawling a few thousand product pages per BigCommerce, Wix or Squarespace shop acceptable, or brand lists only?
5. **Online-first retailers.** Should Cigars Direct (458), Cigar Boulevard (1025), GT Cigars (820), Luxury Cigar Humidors (1499) and Gotham Cigars (880) keep their placement in 'Where to find it', given their feed reflects a web warehouse? This overlaps the storefront audit.

**For other audits**
- **Lapsed Shopify stores counted as working.** Yaxel Cigars (1012) returns HTTP 402 'Store unavailable' from a lapsed Shopify plan (confirmed live), as does Fairway Cigar Lounge (1686). linkCheck records both as 'blocked', which counts as working, so the website audit should treat 402 as dead. It may also be a closure signal.
- **Mislinked websites seen in passing:**
  - 2426 Del Mar Wine & Cigar links bytefederal.com.
  - 928 Nick's Cigar links perdomocigars.com.
  - 3444 House of Cigar & Tobacco links cigar.com.
  - emitcigars.com (5183) lands on a hospital website.
  - 909 and 1464 carry a phone that luckycigar.com doesn't show.
- **Possible duplicate.** 1755 and 2008 (3J's, 4115 S State Road 7 and 7159 Lake Worth Rd) share the phone (561) 868-5600.

**Notes on the evidence**
- The snapshot's timestamps are 7 hours ahead of the API's. Please confirm this comes from the export (TIMESTAMP without a zone read in local time) and not from production.
- The brand-list estimate rests on a biased cached sample plus 9 live sites. A 50-site random sample in the first collect run would tighten it.
- I could not see catalog_pending or the cigars table in the snapshot. That is where the catalog cleanup would size the 'Flavored' and 'Vendor-unknown' style lines beyond the 5 public shelves I checked.

sweeps.fixes: Problems 2, 3 (Wild Bill's and Sweet Fire part), 5 and 6, and the link and placeholder part of 4
sweeps.method:
1) Pull each WPSL feed with a grid of radius-500/max-100 queries until no new store ids appear (9 queries for Wild Bill's, 1 for Sweet Fire). Keep the feed only if at least 80% of its store names carry the chain's brand; that rejects JO's stockist list. Drop other formats by name (Mr. Vapor).
2) Match each unclaimed, non-staff-edited row by the same 10-digit phone (within 30 mi), addressKey plus ZIP/town, or house number plus ZIP within 0.5 mi of OUR pin. Never match on the feed's lat/lng.
3) Write a dry-run decisions file:
(a) Rename a branch's only public row when it lacks the brand AND its phone matches: name = the brand, website = the branch permalink. Address-only matches (Every Day Tobacco, Okemos) go to review.
(b) When 2+ public rows sit on one branch, keep the row whose addressKey equals the feed's (tie-breaks: has hours, overture, lowest id). Hide the others with storefront='duplicate' and reason 'same branch as #X on <host>'; the importer already treats that as binding. Rows at an address on the chain's lounge page whose name says lounge/club/bar are exempt.
(c) Fill feed hours on the kept row when the phone matches: hours_source='website', permalink recorded, locatorDefaultHours guard.
(d) Set has_lounge=1 on the 19 lounge-page addresses.
(e) Rows the chain doesn't list are never hidden on absence alone. Clear their website when it points at the chain host or a redirecting or parked old-brand domain, set staff_edited=1, keep them visible, and queue them for closure review.
(f) Hide only: an address-less name containing '(Coming Soon)' with no branch within 1 mi (#41184), and a row whose address is the OTHER chain's current branch with a different phone (#16646).
4) Staff read every rename and hide (about 30), then apply with --confirm --from.
The importer must be changed FIRST: importStores.js sets name = ? and overwrites address, phone and lat/lng on every re-import of unclaimed directory rows, ignoring staff_edited. Renames would revert on the next deploy.

sweeps.name: Add the missing chain branches from the chains' store locators

sweeps.method:

2) Geocode the street address independently with the US Census Geocoder batch endpoint, falling back to Nominatim at 1 request per second. 3) Insert with source='chain', source_id='<host>:<wpsl id>', the chain's store name, address, zip, phone, website = permalink, feed hours (hours_source='website'), store_type tobacco_shop, confidence 0.55 (same as existing branches), storefront='yes', reason 'listed on <host> store locator <date>', visible=1.

The importer only updates osm/overture rows, and its 150 m twin-merge will attach a later Overture record to the chain row instead of duplicating it. source must be set explicitly, or the importer relabels NULL as 'owner'. sweeps.name: Claim-proof guard (code change plus a nightly verdict per listing)
sweeps.fixes: The dead-domain, stranger-controlled-domain, two-label-domain and chain-mailbox problems. It also removes the misleading staff badge.
sweeps.method:
At claim time the email-code path is allowed only when ALL of these hold. Anything that fails goes to manual review, and the failed reasons are stored on the claim.
(a) A live re-check with linkCheck.checkWebsite() returns 'ok'. 'blocked' goes to staff because the page cannot be read.
(b) The listed URL, the final URL after redirects and the email all have the same registrable domain under the Public Suffix List. Vendor public_suffix_list.dat including its PRIVATE section, so wixsite.com, myshopify.com and github.io count as suffixes.
(c) The domain is not on a deny list: free-mail and ISP hosts (yahoo, aol, gmail, outlook, hotmail, live, msn, icloud, comcast, att, sbcglobal, verizon, bellsouth, earthlink, charter, cox, rr, frontier, juno, tripod), shorteners and directories (goo.gl, g.co, share.google, tinyurl, fb.me, hub.biz, mapquest, eventbrite, yellowpages, cigarplaces, cigarsocialnetwork, webs.com, wix.com, placeweb.site, company.site, beacons.ai, l.ink), anything under .gov, .mil, .edu, *.us locality or k12 or nsn.us, and any non-US ccTLD.
(d) Exactly one public listing uses the domain. Otherwise it is a chain, so staff review it.
(e) The fetched page names the shop. Reuse the hours sweep's matcher (name tokens, phone digits, or street number plus name).
(f) RDAP (rdap.verisign.com for .com and .net, the rdap.org bootstrap for the rest) shows the domain registered at least 365 days ago and not registered after the listing was imported.
(g) contact_email must equal the account email, and that email must be verified through the existing /auth/verify-email flow. Add a unique index so one email can hold one email-verified claim.
Nightly, compute a claim_proof verdict for every public listing ('instant', or a list of reasons) so staff can see the numbers.
On the admin claim card, replace the two-label domainOf badge with the server's verdict and its reasons.
sweeps.sources: stores table, linkCheck.checkWebsite, the vendored Public Suffix List, the hoursSweep name matcher, and free RDAP servers.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: A decision to accept that about two-thirds of claims (2,996 of 4,533 eligible listings on today's data) will need a human. SMTP credentials, which are already on his list. Nothing paid.
sweeps.risk:
A real owner whose site is down, blocked by Cloudflare, shared with sister stores or newly registered waits for staff instead of getting a code. Old registrations that later changed hands (thickercloudz.com, 2016) pass check (f), which is why checks (b) and (e) are required too. Guardrails:
- The guard only removes the self-serve shortcut and never rejects a claim.
- The claimant is told why and what proof staff accept.
- Test against the 25 live examples in this audit: all 12 two-label cases, the 4 named dead domains and the 14 gambling redirects must be refused, and the 5 sampled good domains (jenscigarbar.com, villigercigars.com, cheapcigars4me.com, smokeshopbaltimore.com, bebestobacco.com, all registered 2002-2023) must pass.
sweeps.expected_yield: Measured before RDAP: instant verification stays for 1,537 of 4,533 eligible public listings. 2,996 go to staff: 1,150 dead, 355 redirect away, 1,662 on shared domains, 429 sites that never name the shop, 102 on platforms or directories, 12 on bad suffixes, free-mail or government hosts (these overlap). RDAP then catches re-registrations like gulfportcigars.com (2026-08-17) and puffnstuffcigars.com (2026-05-18).
sweeps.effort: About 1.5 days to build, with self-tests on the examples above. The nightly verdict takes about 20 minutes to run (RDAP at 1 request per second over about 1,000 distinct roots). Review about 1 hour.

sweeps.name: Dead and hijacked website audit (RDAP plus redirect re-check, applied only from a reviewed file)
sweeps.fixes: The dead-domain and stranger-controlled-domain problems at the data level. It also stops the 14 listings that currently link shoppers to gambling sites.
sweeps.method:
1. RDAP every distinct root among public listings with a dead status (692 dns_fail roots plus the not_found, parked, error, refused and timeout ones) and among the 314 that redirect away. Record domain_state: 'unregistered', 'registered_after_import', or 'registered_since_YYYY'.
2. Re-fetch the 314 redirect-away sites. Mark a final URL that is a sale page, a drop-catch lander or a gambling or spam site as a new website_status 'hijacked', which the client treats as dead. Reuse linkCheck's looksParked plus the for-sale and gambling patterns from this audit.
3. Write a decisions file. Unregistered or re-registered domains move to website_prev together with a reason and website is cleared; nothing is deleted, so it can be restored. Hijacked domains become status 'hijacked'.
4. Apply with --from <reviewed file> --confirm, never over claimed or staff_edited rows.
5. The unclaimed banner stops printing a dead domain's name.
sweeps.sources: The snapshot's website and website_final_url fields, free RDAP, and the shops' own sites.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: A decision to clear unregistered links from listings rather than only block them from claims. Nothing else.
sweeps.risk:
This could clear the domain of a shop whose registration merely lapsed and that will renew. Guardrails:
- Clear only on an RDAP 404, or on a registration event after the import date.
- Never touch old registrations whose DNS simply failed (madurostix.com, havanahousecigars.com).
- Keep website_prev so an owner or staff can restore it in one click.
- Staff review the gambling and for-sale list by hand, since it is only about 24 rows.
sweeps.expected_yield: Measured: 24 hijacked or for-sale redirects (10 for sale, 14 gambling), plus up to 314 redirects for review. Estimated: about 450 unregistered .com roots (range 290-560), covering roughly 480 listings, based on 14 of 20 sampled.
sweeps.effort: Half a day to build on linkCheck. About 30 minutes to run. 1-2 hours to review.

sweeps.name: Staff claim review with a visibility guard, a revoke action and hidden-store filters (code)
sweeps.fixes: The staff-approval, no-revoke and hidden-deals problems. It also catches closures on claimed listings through reports.
sweeps.method:
1. approveClaim keeps the current visibility. Un-hiding needs an explicit 'reopen' through the existing /admin/closures/:id/reopen, with its reason shown.
2. Claims on storefront 'duplicate' are refused and pointed at the canonical row, whose id is in storefront_reason.
3. A claim on a hidden row always goes to manual review.
4. /admin/claims returns visible, storefront, storefront_reason, operating_status, closed_reason, website_status, website_final_url, the claim_proof reasons, the number of listings sharing the domain, and the RDAP date. The card shows them.
5. Add POST /admin/stores/:id/unclaim, which sets user_id to NULL, claimed=0 and verified=0 and writes the change to the edit log.
6. Migrate stores.user_id to ON DELETE SET NULL plus claimed=0.
7. admin.js:218 returns 409 'claimed: use unclaim or hide' instead of silently doing nothing.
8. deals.js filters on s.visible=1.
sweeps.sources: Existing tables only.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Nothing, beyond agreeing that approving a claim should not by itself un-hide a listing.
sweeps.risk: No data risk, since this is code that only adds friction for staff. It is dormant until the first claim, so it can ship now.
sweeps.expected_yield: Stops accidental re-publishing of 13,850 verdict-hidden rows, 564 of them closed at the source. Adds a way to undo a wrong claim, which does not exist today.
sweeps.effort: About 1 day, including tests.

sweeps.name: Owner edit log with re-derivation and staged big changes (code)
sweeps.fixes: The owner-edit and template-hours problems, and the dead-link promise on unclaimed banners.
sweeps.method:
1. Add a store_edits table (store_id, user_id, field, before, after, created_at, status, reviewed_by). PUT diffs the request against the row and logs only the fields that changed.
2. Set hours_source='owner' only when the hours actually changed. Remove the HOURS_TEMPLATE pre-fill for existing listings: unknown hours show blank per day and must be typed.
3. Website changed: null website_status, website_final_url and website_checked_at, then call linkCheck.checkStore(id) straight away.
4. Address, city, state or zip changed: geocode with the existing Nominatim helper (at most 1 request per second). If the result is within 2 km of the old pin or inside the new city, update lat, lng and timezone (timeZoneFor). Otherwise apply the text but queue the edit for staff, showing both pins.
5. Stage for staff approval, keeping the old values live meanwhile: a name change sharing no word with the old name, a state change, or a phone in a different area code.
6. POST /stores (owner-created listings) geocodes, runs the dedupe matcher against directory rows within 150 m, and goes to staff when it finds a match.
7. A staff digest of edits, once SMTP is configured.
sweeps.sources: The stores table, Nominatim (free, already used in stores.js:38), linkCheck, storeHours.timeZoneFor and the dedupeListings name matcher.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Decide which fields go live instantly and which wait for staff. The proposal: hours, phone and website go live with re-checks; name, state and large address moves wait for staff.
sweeps.risk: Staging slows real rebrands and moves. Guardrails: only big changes are staged, staff see before and after side by side, and old values stay live until approval, so nothing disappears. A geocoder miss never moves the pin automatically.
sweeps.expected_yield: Every future owner edit gets logged and re-derived. Prevents template hours on the 6,120 public listings with unknown hours. Makes the dead-link fix appear within seconds instead of about 30 days on the 1,323 listings that promise it, and stops stale redirect targets overriding the owner's site on about 371 listings.
sweeps.effort: 1-1.5 days, plus a small review queue tab in AdminPanel.

sweeps.name: Claimed-listing closure watch (job)
sweeps.fixes: The problem of claimed listings receiving no closure evidence.
sweeps.method:
1. The importer records the source's operating_status and closed_reason on claimed rows. It still does not change visibility or any owner fields.
2. closureCheck evaluates claimed rows too, but writes only a review flag, never visible=0. They appear in the Closed queue labelled 'claimed by <account>, last login <date>'.
3. A visitor 'closed' report on a claimed listing enters the same queue and emails the owner.
4. Add an activity check: no owner login for 180 days plus a dead website or a source closure puts the listing in the staff queue and sends a 'still open?' email. With no answer in 30 days, the verified badge and the claimed ranking boost are removed. Visibility changes only by staff decision.
sweeps.sources: The directory file, closureCheck signals, store_reports and users.last_login (to be added if missing).
sweeps.needs_from_mason: SMTP for the owner emails. A decision on whether an absent owner loses the badge.
sweeps.risk: The job never hides anything, so a false signal costs a staff click and one email to a real owner. Guardrail: claimed rows are never auto-hidden, which keeps today's policy.
sweeps.expected_yield: 0 rows today, since nothing is claimed. It keeps closure evidence flowing once claims begin, so a claimed shop cannot become a permanent blind spot.
sweeps.effort: About half a day.

sweeps.name: Make unclaimed profiles honest (copy and UI)
sweeps.fixes: The dead Request button, unread requests, unsent claim emails and wrong data credit.
sweeps.method:
1. Hide the Request tile unless store.claimed=1. Alternatively, build the modal and label it 'we'll pass this to the shop when it joins', with staff able to see request counts for outreach.
2. Make POST /inventory-requests refuse hidden stores.
3. While SMTP is unset, replace 'we will email you' with 'check back on this page', and show a pending-claims badge in the admin nav.
4. Change the banner credit to 'Overture Maps Foundation and OpenStreetMap contributors'.
5. Show the 'inventory appears once claimed' line only when there is no web-read menu.
6. Hide the follow notification options on unclaimed listings, since nobody can post there.
sweeps.sources: Client code only.
sweeps.needs_from_mason: Decide whether requests on unclaimed listings should be collected as outreach material or the tile simply hidden.
sweeps.risk: None to data.
sweeps.expected_yield: Removes a dead button from 7,431 public profiles. Corrects the data credit on 6,887 Overture-sourced listings and the inventory line on 43. Stops promising emails that cannot be sent.
sweeps.effort: About 2 hours.

gaps.already_covered:
Already handled, and handled well:
- Nineteen shared hosts (facebook, instagram, wixsite, weebly, square.site, business.site, godaddysites, squarespace, wordpress, blogspot, google.com and others) can never verify instantly (claims.js SHARED_HOSTS).
- Claim security basics: a 10 per hour per IP limit on claim and verify, codes bcrypt-hashed with a 30-minute expiry, 5 wrong guesses burn the code, a 2-minute resend cooldown, and a fallback to staff review when mail fails to send (WORKLOG, Interruption 1).
- A self-serve claim does not un-hide a staff-hidden listing.
- Protection of claimed and staff-edited rows is consistent everywhere: the importer skips them, closureCheck, chainCheck and dedupeListings exclude them, the hours sweep's apply step refuses claimed, staff-edited and owner-set hours at write time, and visitor 'closed' reports never auto-hide them. The importer honours storefront verdicts.
- linkCheck already hides dead links from shoppers and rechecks claimed rows first. Its checkStore(id) exists and can be called after an owner edit.
- The hours sweep already has a 'site never names this shop' matcher (432 skips), reusable as claim proof.
- Claimants are emailed on approval or rejection once SMTP is set.
- The Closed queue's confirm and reopen actions set staff_edited so later runs keep the decision.
- The owner's menu refresh has private-IP refusal and a cooldown.

None of that is in question. The gaps are in what counts as proof of ownership, what a claim unlocks, and what happens after the claim.
gaps.open_questions:
1. Throughput versus safety: is sending about two-thirds of claims (2,996 of 4,533 eligible) to staff acceptable at launch volume? No real claim has been made yet.
2. Chains: should one account be able to manage several listings (a brand account), given that wildbillstobacco.com covers 203 listings and the one-store-per-account rule forces one account per branch?
3. Which owner edits go live instantly and which wait for staff: name, state, a large address move, the website?
4. Should unregistered or re-registered website domains be cleared from listings (reversibly, into website_prev), or only blocked from claims? Clearing also removes the dead-domain text from the unclaimed banner.
5. What proof do staff accept for manual claims? Today the reviewer gets only a message box and a flawed 'matches website domain' badge. Options: a call-back to the listed phone, a mailed code, a screenshot of the Google Business Profile.
6. Should inventory requests on unclaimed listings be collected for outreach ('12 people asked for X at your shop') or the tile hidden?
7. The directory has no 'as-of' date per record: every row's created_at is the 2026-09-10 import. Should buildDirectory extract Overture's sources[].update_time, so the RDAP guard can compare a domain's registration with when the source last saw it?
8. Should an owner who stops logging in lose the verified badge and the claimed ranking boost after a set period?
9. Assumption to confirm: production runs master as of commit 3f79e7a. The code paths were read in the repo, not probed on the live API, to keep this audit read-only.

gaps.current_state:
No job reads a licence registry today. ROADMAP.md names them as the validation layer, but none of closureCheck, storefrontCheck, chainCheck, dedupeListings or linkCheck uses one. stores.last_verified_at exists but is null on all 7,431 public listings; only the claim flow sets it.

REGISTRIES CHECKED 2026-09-10. All are free with no key, and all were downloaded to work/lic/:
- NYC DCWP Tobacco Retail Dealer (from the brief): 6,707 records (3,516 active, 3,191 expired, surrendered, revoked or suspended). Has phone, lat/lng and expiry dates. Updated daily.
- NY State Tax, data.ny.gov 55xf-9jat: 22,095 current registrations (13,691 cigarette/tobacco, 8,404 vape). Has DBA, suspension dates and coordinates. Lists current registrants only, so a closure shows up only as absence.
- NY State DOH, health.data.ny.gov 9ma3-vsuk: 18,022 active vendors with a subcategory (TOBACCO RETAIL 1,536; BAR/LOUNGE 643). The last run was 2026-01-23, so it is 8 months old.
- Texas Comptroller, data.texas.gov yrkr-maw5 (all) and n4rp-ar9b (active): 90,534 permits, 59,505 active and 31,029 inactive. Has outlet (DBA) name, taxpayer id and begin/end dates. Updated daily (begin dates run to 2026-09-11). No phone or coordinates. 7,042 inactive permits have no end date.
- Florida DBPR (the earlier search that found only an application form missed these): bdTOBlic.csv has 31,571 retail tobacco permits, bd4012lic.csv has 7,779 standalone ones, and bd400lic.csv holds 198,387 licences of all kinds. Last-modified today. Has DBA, location, status codes, expiry and a Smoking Designation field. Only current, escrow and delinquent permits are listed, so a lapsed permit is simply missing.
- California CDTFA LR-CA-Statewide.xlsx: 23,598 licensed retailers as of 2026-09-03, updated monthly. Has DBA and address but no status. By law it leaves out sole proprietors.
- Pennsylvania DOR, data.pa.gov ut72-sft8: 17,079 active licences, 15,609 of them retail. Has trade name and coordinates, refreshed daily. Cancelled licences are removed.
- Chicago BACP: 1,937 current Tobacco licences (uupf-x98q), plus 9,032 history rows since 2023 (r5kz-chrr) with cancelled (AAC) and revoked (REV) statuses, dates and account numbers.
- Washington LCB CIG_TOB_VAPE_021026.xlsx: 15,728 endorsements at 5,912 business addresses, with phone. A snapshot from 2026-02-10.

NO BULK FILE FOUND:
- NJ: the licence is issued by DORES and there is no public list.
- MD: retail licences sit with county clerks; ATCC lists only manufacturers and wholesalers.
- MI and NC: no state retail licence exists (MI holds 447 public listings, NC 354).
- VA: publishes a distributor list only.
- OH: county auditors issue the licences.
- GA: none found.
- Per Avior's state table: KS, LA, MA, MO, SC and ND offer lookups only; CO (2022), KY (2023), OR (2023) and UT publish PDFs.
- Philadelphia publishes a permit dataset; it was not downloaded because PA's state list covers the city.

COVERAGE: 2,850 of 7,431 public listings (38.4%) sit where a bulk file exists: FL 848, CA 553, TX 549, PA 420, NY 322, WA 119, Chicago 39.

JOIN (work/lic/match.js and classify.js):
- Rules: phone match; or same ZIP or town, plus house number, plus a shared street word after normalising (37-12 becomes 3712, Fifth becomes 5, 73rd becomes 73, suite and unit stripped); or within 60 m with the names agreeing.
- Names are compared on distinctive words, ignoring legal suffixes and generic trade words.

Results for the 2,850 covered public listings:
- 1,339 (47%): an active licence in the same business's name.
- 406 (14%): the only active licence at the door belongs to another name. These are mostly strip-mall neighbours or corporate names. Only 35 cases have a suite number on both sides.
- 185: the same name is licensed at another address in the ZIP. This is noisy because town words match.
- 101 (TX 84, Chicago 10, NYC 7): only inactive licences in our name at our address. In 28 of them a different business now holds the active licence there.
- 17: only another business's inactive licence.
- 802 (28%): no licence found. By state: FL 252/848, CA 218/553 (sole proprietors missing from the file), PA 117/420, NY 90/322, TX 80/549, WA 38/119, Chicago 7/39. Of these 802, 110 have no street number to match on, and 68 carry company-style names (Oliva Tobacco Co, C.L.E. Cigar Company, Sosa Cigar Company). I did not web-check whether those are non-retail.

RECALL (work/lic/missing.js): 1,763 active licence locations have a cigar-type word in the name, counted once per jurisdiction and address after dropping mobile, VIN, online and PO-box entries.
- 975 match a public listing and 171 match only hidden rows.
- 601 have no row among the 42,923 within phone, address, 80 m or the same name in the same town. 513 of those have CIGAR, TOBACCONIST or HUMIDOR in the name; 226 of those 513 look like storefronts by name and address.

VERIFIED ON THE WEB: 23 searches.

problems.title: Closed shops still public; the licence lapse caught what Overture missed
problems.affected_public: Measured: 101 public listings in TX, NYC and Chicago have only inactive licences in their own name at their address. I checked 12: 1 closed, 3 renamed or replaced, 2 moved, 1 probably moved, 3 open and 2 unresolved. That puts roughly 45 to 65 of the 101 in the wrong state, but plain closures were only 1 of 12; most are renames or moves. FL, CA, PA, NYS and WA publish no inactive records, so there a lapse shows only as absence (part of the 802 unmatched).
problems.how_measured: match.js and classify.js (classes B and C), then closure2.js to sort them by second signals: own-site hours 6, live website 25, dead website 16, no website 22, inactive with no end date 14, same name elsewhere 18. I used web search on Yelp, the shop's own site and Waze.
examples: #5465 Winston's Cigar Lounge, 2426 Times Blvd, Houston. The TX permit ended 2026-01-12 and the shop closed on January 12 after 63 years (Pipe Smokers Den thread; houston.winstonscigarlounge.com). Overture still says open and the listing is public. CONFIRMED.

#5267 Stogies World Class Cigars, Houston. Its only TX permit (2009) is INACTIVE with no end date, yet its own site and Yelp (June 2026) show it trading. CONFIRMED FALSE POSITIVE: an inactive permit with no end date proves nothing.
#5593 BlackHouse Cigars, Spring TX. Permit inactive since 2023-12-31, but its site (hours read today) and Yelp show it open. CONFIRMED FALSE POSITIVE.

#41493 Manhattan Tobacco, 881 9th Ave NYC. DCWP licence expired 2024-12-31, no website, but Yelp (July 2026) shows it open 24 hours. CONFIRMED FALSE POSITIVE. 'No website' is not a second signal, and NYC has many smoke shops trading without a licence.
#2261 House of Havana, Odessa. Permit ended 2026-04-15 and houseofhavana.net returns NXDOMAIN today, but Yelp's page was updated June 2026 and does not say closed. UNRESOLVED.
#16372 Lincoln Park Tobacconist, Chicago. The licence for the 2025-26 term was cancelled (AAC) on 2026-07-20; Yelp was updated Aug 2026 and does not say closed. UNRESOLVED.
problems.customer_impact: The map sends people to a lounge that has been shut for 8 months (Winston's). The registry dated the closure to the day, while Overture, the website check and the contact check all missed it.

problems.title: Renamed or replaced shops still showing the old name
problems.affected_public: Measured: 24 public listings where a different business now holds the active licence for our exact suite, or our name's licence lapsed and another took the door. 15 are suite matches and 9 lapsed; 2 are both. About 5 of the 24 are spelling or truncation variants of the same business ('UNLIMTED', 'SHRADDHA ENTERPRISES INC - CIGAR CR'). I checked 4 and all 4 were renamed.

sweeps.name: Registry review queue for closures, renames and moves (never auto-hide)
